column1: 7. Create API end point to find fraud screening request which reached timeout
column47:
*Why:* if fraud screening request reached timeout (Kafka message from OFD broker wasn't received in time), such fraud screening requests need to be found and processed
*When:* 
*Where:* core-payment-batch-handler-data-manager 
*What:*

Create API end point fraud-screening-request/timeout

Incoming parameters - none.

API end point actions:
 * find one fraud screening request with status FS_SENT which has response_timeout_dtime < current dtime (take with oldest response_timeout_dtime) 
 * if fraud screening request is found, update status of it to "FS_PROCESSING", response_type = "TIMEOUT"

API end point results:
 * Fraud screening SID
 * Transaction ID
 * OR "Nothing found"  if there are no fraud screening requests found.

column1: 10. Update API end point updating data for fraud screening request
column47:
*Why:* Response to fraud screening request will be received via API call. It is needed to calculate when to call response API
*When:* 
*Where:* batch handler data manager
*What:*

API: [/v1/core-payment-batch-handler-data-manager/fraud-screening-request/update|https://core-payment-batch-handler-data-manager-dev.apps.scp-west-zone01-z02.swedbank.io/swagger-ui/index.html#/Fraud%20screening/updateFraudScreening]

API endpoint fields:
 * fraud screening SID - mandatory
 * transaction_id - optional
 * request_sent_dtime - optional
 * amount_of_payments - optional
 * response_received_dtime - optional
 * response_code - optional
 * response_type - optional
 * status - mandatory
 * no_with_response_allow - optional
 * no_with_response_decline - optional
 * no_with_response_unknown - optional
 * no_with_response_not_received - optional

API endpoint actions:
 * store data provided
 * do not allow to overwrite response_type, transaction_id - if they were already stored, API response should be failure.{color:#ff8b00} If provided transaction_id value is the same as currently stored - do not throw an error.{color}
 * if request_sent_dtime is provided, calculate response_timeout_dtime and store it. Calculation:  request_sent_dtime + time from table
 * validate that response_type is either "TIMEOUT" or "KAFKA_MSG" (other values not allowed)

 

API endpoint validations:
 * If transaction_id is provided, status and{color:#ff8b00} (request_sent_dtime or response_received_dtime){color} are mandatory

 

API endpoint response:
 * success
 * failure

Update storing ** payment information, done with EASYPAY-843:

Store information about the payments by calling API payment/create with values:

 * Signing batch SID -  response from batch creation API (same SID as batch SID), has to be provided only for signed batches (that is, if together with file, signature information was received)

 * Reporting status:

 * Original Instruction Identification - from file
 * Original End To End Identification - from file
 * Original Transaction Reference - from file
 * Requested Execution Date - from file
 * Country code - from file
 * Instructed amount - from file
 * Debtor name - from file
 * Debtor account number - from file
 * Creditor name - from file
 * Creditor account number - from file
 * {color:#ff8b00}Creditor account type - from file. If IBAN provided - IBAN. If other - OTHER.{color}

*Create* a new procedure *MDM_DAY0_LOADING_SO* in a new package PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.{*}MDM_DAY0_GENERATION{*} (PAYRUN-1515) in CORE DBs (LT, EE, LV)

The new procedure must be able to:
 * select a batch of product agreement data from PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.{*}MDM_INITIAL_AGREEMENTS{*} table (PAYRUN-1420) where *ready_for_sending = Y* and {*}type='STANDING_ORDER_AGREEMENT'{*};
 * for each selected record to call procedure PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.MDM_PAYLOAD_MESSAGE_GENERATION.{*}MDM_AGREEMENT_SO{*} (PAYRUN-1463);
 * for each sent record to set PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.{*}MDM_INITIAL_AGREEMENTS.placed_in_AQ{*} = (database sysdate) and set *ready_for_sending = S* (meaning record is created in AQ table)

+Result of this procedure execution:+
 * all records in PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.{*}MDM_INITIAL_AGREEMENTS{*} for which *type='STANDING_ORDER_AGREEMENT'* and *ready_for_sending* value previously was set to *Y*
 ** must have filled columns *placed_in_AQ* filled with *sysdate* and *ready_for_sending* value set to *S*
 ** then each record from PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.{*}MDM_INITIAL_AGREEMENTS{*}
 *** must have record in AQ table "PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.{*}MDM_MESSAGES{*}"

PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.{*}MDM_MESSAGES{*} records format:

  "instanceId": "",             // DYNAMIC VALUE - (string)- use "EE", "LT", "LV" as value based on engagement origin country context
  "type": "",                   // STATIC VALUE - (string) - use "ENGAGEMENT" as value
  "lastModifiedTimestamp": ,    // DYNAMIC VALUE - (long timestamp) - use CREBIT.PER_MK CHANGED_DATE table column value, format: unix timestamp milliseconds, sys_extract_utc
  "operation": "",              // STATIC VALUE - (string) use "INSERT" as value
  "payload": {                  // (object) Details of the change
    "engagementSourceRef": "",  // DYNAMIC VALUE - (string) - use "CREBIT.PER_MK[PMK_NR]",  Format: <shema_name>.<table_name>[<unique record_id>]         
    "type": "",                 // STATIC VALUE - (string) - use "STANDING_ORDER" as value
    "status": "",               // DYNAMIC VALUE - (string) - use CREBIT.PER_MK STAATUS table column value
    "nr": "",                   // DYNAMIC VALUE - (string) - use CREBIT.PER_MK PMK_NR table column value      
    "startDate": ,              // DYNAMIC VALUE - (long timestamp) - use CREBIT.PER_MK KEHT_AKP, format: unix timestamp milliseconds, sys_extract_utc
    "endDate": ,                // DYNAMIC VALUE - (long timestamp) - use CREBIT.KEHT_LKP (date set by client when his agreement ends) or CREBIT.PER_MK ANNUL_KP (manual cancellation of ongoing agreement) or can be NULL (until manual cancellation), format: unix timestamp milliseconds, sys_extract_utc

      {
        "roleSourceRef": "",    // DYNAMIC VALUE - (string) - use CREBIT.PER_MK[PMK_NR] Format: <shema_name>.<table_name>[<unique record_id>].
        "partyId": "",          // DYNAMIC VALUE - (string) NULL

17.02.2026 14:29;p997cfe;* *CREBIT.KEHT_LKP* (date set by client when his agreement ends)
 * *NULL* (until manual cancellation)
 * *CREBIT.PER_MK ANNUL_KP* (manual cancellation of ongoing agreement)

USE CASES:

*END DATE IS SPECIFIED*
 # go to ibank create standing order agreement
 # specify end date for it 
 # sign agreement 
 # the payload should contain i_dt_till = CREBIT.PER_MK KEHT_LKP

*NO END DATE FOR AGREEMENT*
 # go to ibank create standing order agreement
 # don't specify end date for it 
 # sign agreement 
 # the payload should contain i_dt_till = NULL 

*NO END DATE SPECIFIED, BUT LATER CANCELLED*
 # go to ibank create standing order agreement
 # don't specify end date for it 
 # sign agreement 
 # the payload should contain i_dt_till = NULL 
 # go to ibank manully close agreement (cancel this agreement) 
 # the payload now should contain i_dt_till = CREBIT.PER_MK  ANNUL_KP;;;

 * Select product agreements data based on input parameters
 * Format selected agreement data to [Engagementpayload|https://wiki.swedbank.net/display/BCD/Topic+payloads#expand-Engagementpayload] message format (to call procedure PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.MDM_PAYLOAD_MESSAGE_GENERATION.MDM_AGREEMENT_SO described in PAYRUN-1463)

column1: DB: create table to store session information
column47:
*Why:* as fraud screening request will be sent from BH instead of iBank (as is now), session information has to be stored for it to be accessible to BH (session information is mandatory in fraud screening request)
*When:* 
*Where:* Core DB
*What:*

Create new table in payments schema: PAYMENTS.BATCH_SESSION_INFO

Grant rights for the table to PAYMENT_SUP and PAYMENT_RO

 

!image-2026-02-03-10-53-23-508.png!

 
|*Field*|*Comment*|
|SID|Unique identifier. Sequence|
|Channel|INP for private iBank, THN for corporate iBank|
|Application_menu|Place where payments were signed. Possible values: "list_pmnt", "file_import", "mass_pmnt"|
|Application_language|Display language code|
|Account_owner_id|Core id of the account owner|
|Account_owner_type|P - private, C - corporate|
|Debtor_acc_id|Internal account number from which payments were initiated|
|Number_of_trxs|Number of payments signed together in the session|
|Control_sum|Total of all individual amounts of signed payments, irrespective of currencies|
|Mass_pmnt_header_id|Reference to crebit.dp_out_mass_pmt|
|Request_path|Path to the page where payments were signed|
|Identification_method|Method with which customer identified themselves when signing into application|
|Signing_method|Method with which customer signed payments|
|Signer_user_id|User id (from teleagreement) which signed payments|
|Session_key|Session key|
|Device_id|Value of hanza cookie (always exists in iBank)|
|IP_address|IP address|
|Web_session_user_agent|Browser and operating system of the customer|
|Web_session_start_dtime|Timestamp when customer logged into iBank|

column47:
*Why:* Fraud screening requests and responses for batches will be handled in Batch handler. Batches to be sent for screening will be sent to Batch handler via AQ

*What:*

Create queue to store batch information which will be read by Batch handler

 * queue_name => PAYMENTS.Q_CH_SIGNED_PMNT_BATCH
 * queue_table => PAYMENTS.Q_CH_SIGNED_PMNT_BATCH_MSG

 * queue_payload_type => SYS.AQ$_JMS_TEXT_MESSAGE
 * Retry - 5
 * Delay - 10 secs

 

Select should be granted to PAYMENT_SUP and PAYMENT_RO

 

Data which must be inserted in to queue:
 * Country code
 * Channel
 * Session id
 * Account owner id
 * Mass payment header id
 * Number of payments
 * Total amount
 * Application_menu (list_pmnt, file_import, mass_pmnt)

column1: Implement payment file recovery process - validating batches
column47:
*Why:* if payment file parsing and payment initiation failed, payment file recovery process needs to check at which step payment file parsing and payment initiation failed and then proceed accordingly 
*When:* 
*Where:* worker-payment-batch-handler
*What:*

As this is recovery process - it has to reuse as many elements of original process, so that no action would be duplicated in the application (easier maintenance later).

 

Continuation of process PAYRUN-2850 if payment file has status "Validated"

Process:
 # Call API end point to get all batches registered for that payment file (API end point created with PAYRUN-2846)
 # For each batch from the payment file parsing - check if it's registered in database (based on response from API in first step) and its status:
 ## Not registered - start payment file parsing process (see second diagram) from "Batch creation needed"
 ## Status "Rejected" - call API end point to get all status responses for the batch (API end point created with PAYRUN-2829)
 ### Status response exists - end process for the batch
 ### Status response does not exist - initiate creation of pain.002 (reuse process done with PAYME-1058)
 ## Status "Registered"
 ### Validate batch (reuse process done with EASYPAY-899)
 ### For valid batch (not valid will get rejected in validation process):
 #### Split batch to payments (reuse EASYPAY-843 - no need to store payments)
 #### Call API end point batch/\{batchSID}/payments (created with PAYRUN-2835)
 #### If it's not mass payment - proceed with process in PAYRUN-2852, if it's mass payment - check if API end point batch/\{batchSID}/payments (created with PAYRUN-2835) returns at least one payment:
 ##### If it does - proceed with process in  PAYRUN-2852
 ##### If it does not - publish mass payment header information to Kafka topic w990.batch.handler.payment.order, then proceed with process in  PAYRUN-2852

 

Also: update main process - if it was initiated from recovery, at the end of process update recovery status (see second diagram)

 

Comparing the data to identify the batch:
 * payment_info_id has to be the same

column47:
*Why:* if payment file parsing and payment initiation failed, payment file recovery process needs to check at which step payment file parsing and payment initiation failed and then proceed accordingly 
*When:*

*What:*

As this is recovery process - it has to reuse as many elements of original process, so that no action would be duplicated in the application (easier maintenance later).

 

Process:
 # Read Kafka topic (created with SMARTPAY-850), filter out recovery_type = "PAYMENT_FILE"
 # Call API end point [incoming-file/\{sid}|https://core-payment-batch-handler-data-manager-dev.apps.scp-west-zone01-z02.swedbank.io/swagger-ui/index.html#/Payment%20batch%20handler%20data%20manager%20incoming%20file/getIncomingFile]
 # Check status of payment file:
 ## If status is "Registered" - start payment file parsing process (see second diagram) from "Payment file needed" and call API (created with SMARTPAY-867) to update recovery status to "RPF_INITIATED". Then end process.
 ## If status is "Validated":
 ### Get payment file from filebarn (reuse what was done with EASYPAY-844)
 ### Split file to batches (reuse what was done with EASYPAY-847 - no need to store info)
 ### Call API (created with SMARTPAY-867) to update recovery status to "RPF_INITIATED"
 ### Process for batch continued in story PAYRUN-2851 and for payments - in story PAYRUN-2852
 ### After all payments in all batches were processed - call API end point [incoming-file/process-related-statuses|https://core-payment-batch-handler-data-manager-dev.apps.scp-west-zone01-z02.swedbank.io/swagger-ui/index.html#/Payment%20batch%20handler%20data%20manager%20incoming%20file/processPaymentFileRelatedStatuses]
 ### Call API (created with SMARTPAY-867) to update recovery status to "RPF_COMPLETED" and end process.
 ## If status is "Rejected"
 ### Call API end point PAYRUN-2829 to get status report data
 #### If status report exists - call API (created with SMARTPAY-867) to update recovery status to "RPF_NOT_NEEDED" and end process.
 #### If it does not exist:
 ##### Get payment file from filebarn (reuse what was done with EASYPAY-844)

*Why:* To use existing logic to validate and enrich instant/normal SEPA, Intrabanks and Cross Border payments
*When:* When request is received from FLM
*Where:* Payment services
*What:*
 * Create new RPC to validate and enrich instant/normal SEPA, Intrabanks and Cross Border payments
 * Use PODM JSON structure as an input for validation
 * Use the new DB procedure created (or updated) in EASYPAY-909 to validate non-SEPA Cross Border payments
 * Output shall consist of:
 ** error code (if any)
 ** Full PODM structure w/o warnings
 * No save mode should be used by the endpoint
 * The validation code should be re-used
 * {color:#de350b}Add Grant execute on PAYMENTS.FPO_PAYMENT to pms_user{color}

*API description:* [Payment Services: FLM supporting Service endpoints|https://wiki.swedbank.net/spaces/DPAY/pages/2250138228/Payment+Services+FLM+supporting+Service+endpoints]

{*}PODM JSON structure and mappings{*}{*}:{*} *[Payment Order Data Manager JSON structure.xlsx|https://myntet.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/teams/PaymentsBaltic/Delade%20dokument/Analysis%20and%20architecture/Payments%20Mapping%20to%20ISO%20Elements/Payment%20Order%20Data%20Manager%20JSON%20structure.xlsx?d=w6c9d1db06f5e470ebd740697eb46ab2f&csf=1&web=1&e=ZbXcJe]*
h4. *Test Scope*

AC1 should be tested for the following payment types (routes):

CRE  Intrabank payment, internal crediting
SEPO  SEPA outgoing domestic payment
SIPO  SEPA outgoing domestic instant payment
RTGS  Domestic outgoing payment to RTGS
SEPCO  SEPA outgoing cross-border payment
SEPGO  SEPA outgoing intragroup payment
SIPCO  SEPA outgoing cross-border instant payment
FPO International payment
h2. Acceptance Criteria

*AC1: Successful Validation*

*GIVEN* a request is made to validate and enrich payment with a PODM structure to the payment services new RPC endpoint validate_and_enrich
*WHEN* the validation is successful
*AND* procedures enriched any of the attributes in the payload
*THEN* the response contains full PODM structure

*AC2: Successful Validation with warnings*

*GIVEN* a request is made to validate and enrich payment with a PODM structure to the payment services new RPC endpoint validate_and_enrich
*AND* the PODM structure already has existing warnings in the payload
*WHEN* the validation was successful
*AND* warning was triggered
*THEN* the response should return PODM payload 
*AND* existing warnings are not overridden in PODM request payload
*AND* the response should have existing and new warnings

*AC3: Unsuccessful Validation*

*GIVEN* a request is made to validate and enrich payment  with a PODM structure to the payment services new RPC endpoint validate_and_enrich
*WHEN* the validation is not successful
*THEN* the response contains an error code in dp error code format

*AC4: Successful Validation Without Attribute Updates/enrichment*

*GIVEN* a request is made to validate and enrich payment with a PODM structure to the payment services new RPC endpoint validate_and_enrich
*WHEN* the validation is successful but no attributes need to be enriched/updated
*THEN* the response contains full PODM structure

column1: Create possibility to fake file upload from SGW
column47:
*Why:* Testing file upload through SGW is not possible, therefore we need to fake getting the file.
*When:* 
*Where:* 
*What:* 

Create application which would
 * upload payment file to filebarn with file type INCOMING_PAYMENT_FILE and Customer ID as Owner ID
 * publish payment file information to Kafka topic w990.batch.handler.incoming.files

 

What information has to be provided by user:
 * XML file - Mandatory
 * Country code - string- Mandatory
 * Customer ID - string - Mandatory
 * Tracking ID - string- Mandatory
 * Web session IP address - string - Mandatory
 * Agreement ID - long - Mandatory
 * Signature information (list, not limited): - Optional
 ** Order of signing - integer - Mandatory
 ** Country code - string - Mandatory
 ** Core ID - string - Mandatory
 ** Accounts (list, not limited) - Mandatory
 *** Account number - string

Information which is always the same:
 * Channel - SGW
 * File storage - FILEBARN
 * Storage type ID - INCOMING_PAYMENT_FILE

Information derived from other data:
 * Storage owner ID - use Customer ID
 * File ID - result from uploading file to filebarn

column1: Create Ksql STREAM for selecting data to Flow Manager dedicated topic
column47:
*Why:* KsqlDB allows to provide only required information from Raw topic to Flow Manager dedicated topic.

*When:* any time
*Where:* kafka
*What:*   Create STREAM bpay_flow_manager_stream

the following fields need to be selected into stream from raw topic and put into flow manager dedicated topic (EASYPAY-999):

PaymentOrderMetaData
 * holder_channel_code
 * in_channel_code
 * out_channel_code
 * status
 * error_code
 * payment version
 * warnings
 * country_code

PaymentOrder
 * payment_id 

filter criteria/conditions:
 * in_channel_code{color:#172b4d}='HGW' *OR* related_doc_type_code in ('LIST','MM', 'FILE'){color}
 * LAST_UPDATED_BY_APP <> 'FLOW_MANAGER' 

{color:#172b4d}(related_doc_type_code and LAST_UPDATED_BY_APP - not in the row topic data model. should be included with separate task CALLS-1174, CALLS-1175) {color}

kafka message key = PaymentOrder.payment_id  (DP.ID)

 

for more information about streams visit this page : [https://www.confluent.io/blog/how-real-time-stream-processing-works-with-ksqldb/?_ga=2.46309935.906919299.1729078839-1420397618.1729078839]

column1: Set XKONT value for new Ledger Accounts
column47:
*Why:* VAT Law changes in LT
*When:* 
*Where:* set-up of Ledger Accounts in table CREBIT.KONTOD 
*What:* 

The Back Office has created new ledger accounts for SWIFT service VAT. column47:
*Why:* To use existing logic to decide on priority and out channel code
*When:* When request is sent from FLM
*Where:* Payment services
*What:* 
 * Create the RPC to use existing logic for priority and out channel code
 * PODM attribute structure to be used for the request, mappings provided in the table below

*RPC description:* [Payment Services: FLM supporting Service endpoints|https://wiki.swedbank.net/spaces/DPAY/pages/2250138228/Payment+Services+FLM+supporting+Service+endpoints]

{*}PODM JSON structure and mappings{*}{*}:{*} *[Payment Order Data Manager JSON structure.xlsx|https://myntet.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/teams/PaymentsBaltic/Delade%20dokument/Analysis%20and%20architecture/Payments%20Mapping%20to%20ISO%20Elements/Payment%20Order%20Data%20Manager%20JSON%20structure.xlsx?d=w6c9d1db06f5e470ebd740697eb46ab2f&csf=1&web=1&e=ZbXcJe]*

Input parameters:
 
|Path, level 1|Path, level 2|Path, level 3|Path, level 4|Path, level 5|Path, level 6|Field name|DB Table|DB Field|Usage|
|/pmtInf/|cdtTrfTxInf/|pmtTpInf/|svcLvl/| | |cd|DP_ISO|SERVICE_LEVEL_CODE|for priority|
|/pmtInf/|cdtTrfTxInf/|pmtTpInf/|lclInstrm/| | |cd|DP_ISO|LOCAL_INSTRUMENT_CODE |for priority|
|/pmtInf/|cdtTrfTxInf/|pmtTpInf/|lclInstrm/| | |prtry|DP_ISO|LOCAL_INSTRUMENT_PROPRIETARY|for priority|
|/pmtInf/|cdtTrfTxInf/|pmtTpInf/|ctgyPurp/| | |cd| | | |
|/pmtInf/|cdtTrfTxInf/| | | | |instdAmtCcy|DP|CURRENCY|for priority and out-channel|
|/pmtInf/|pties/|cdtr/|acct/|id/| |iban|DP|CREDITOR_ACC_NUMBER|for priority and out-channel|
|/pmtInf/|pties/|cdtr/|acct/|id/|othr/|id|DP|CREDITOR_ACC_NUMBER| |
|/pmtInf/|cdtTrfTxInf/| | | | |instdAmt|DP|AMOUNT|for out-channel|
|/bkIntPrtryInf/|procgInf/| | | | |valDt|DP|VALUE_DATE|for out-channel|

Output parameters:
 * bkIntPrtryInf/procgInf/errCd (in case of error)
/bkIntPrtryInf/procgInf/docPrty
/bkIntPrtryInf/procgInf/outChnlCd

Mapping rules:
 * for Intrabank, Swedbank group payments in other currency than EUR and where the payment is mapped as SEPA and priority is INST we set the priority as LT, EE as Ordinary and LV economy
 * for Swedbank group payments in EUR, mass payment, where it is set as SEPA and priority is INST we set the priority as Instant
 * If the priority is set as INST and the payment is among Baltic countries and beneficiary bank is not reachable as INST then we REJECT
 * If the priority is set as INST and the payment is to SWED Sweden or Norway and the bank is not reachable as INST then we REJECT

h3. Acceptance Criteria
h3. *AC1: Payment Priority Calculation and out channel code*

*GIVEN* the following inputs from table above are provided to the RPC endpoint:
*WHEN* the RPC endpoint is called to use existing logic for priority and out channel code calculation
*THEN* the response will include the Payment priority attribute or out channel code
h3. -*AC2: Out Channel Code*-

-*GIVEN* the following inputs are provided to the RPC endpoint:-
-Currency-
-Creditor account number-
-Amount-
-In Channel Code-
-Charger bearer-
-*WHEN* the RPC endpoint is called and existing logic for out channel code calculation is used-
-*THEN* the response will include the Out channel code attribute-
h3. *AC3: Error Handling*

*GIVEN* any of the inputs for AC1 or AC2
*WHEN* there is an error in processing the request
*THEN* the response will include a textual error code
h3. *AC4: Payment Priority Calculation for Mass payment header*

*GIVEN* a mass payment header provided to the RPC endpoint:
*AND* Local instrument code is provided as INST
*WHEN* the RPC endpoint is called to use existing logic for priority calculation
*THEN* priority will be set as instant

column1: Update API which updates batch and file status
column47:
*Why:* Once pain.002 report is sent, batch and payment statuses have to reflect that
*When:* 
*Where:* core-payment-batch-handler-data-manager 
*What:*

Update API created with EASYPAY-1028 - it has to work even when batch has no payments in it. (use case: batch validation failed, batch status was updated to B_REJECTED, no payments were parsed from the batch)

 

API actions - update according to descriptions below (red shows new changes, cross-out parts show what should be removed). In case there are no payments in the batch, skip that step:
 # Collect all batches in the file. For each batch:
 ## Check status of all payments in the batch:
 ### If there exists at least one payment with status "P_REGISTERED" - provide error as API response
 ### If there exists at least one payment with status "P_PROCESSING" - update batch status to "B_PROCESSING"

column1: iBank Private and Business PB: Showing warning messages in case customer disabled instant payments or exceeded instant payment, daily and/or monthly limits in SMART payment form
column47:
*Why:*
 * According to [Instant Payments Regulation|https://www.ecb.europa.eu/paym/integration/retail/instant_payments/html/instant_payments_regulation.en.html] and [2025 EPC Payment Scheme Rulebooks,|https://www.europeanpaymentscouncil.eu/news-insights/news/revised-entry-force-dates-2025-epc-payment-scheme-rulebooks-and-version-10-epc] payment service providers (PSPs) must to offer for all private and corporate customers (payment service users - PSU) two new payment limits: 
 ** Instant payment daily limit.
 ** Instant payment transaction limit.
 * As agreed with PB daily banking lawyers, instant payment daily/ transaction limits must be calculated in customer's permanent payment daily and monthly limits.

column47:
*Why:* Publish payment information to Kafka topic so that Payment flow manager would get payment information and would be able to start processing the payments
*When:* 
*Where:* worker-payment-batch-handler  
*What:*

After payment is registered (EASYPAY-843) then:
 # Publish to the topic w990.batch.handler.payment.orders.
 # Call API EASYPAY-894 to update payment status = 'PROCESSING'

 

Publishing to Kafka topic logic:

Header - information from related system:

Key: related_system -> code 
Value: related_sytem -> reference

proprietary_information:
 * country_code - from Kafka topic EASYPAY-827
 * originating_information -> in_channel_code  - from Kafka topic EASYPAY-827 (channel)
 * related_system -> code - PBH_HID (means that it's batch SID)
 * related_sytem -> reference - from EASYPAY-847 (batch SID)
 * related_system -> code - PBH_ID (means that it's payment SID)
 * related_sytem -> reference - from EASYPAY-843 (payment SID)
 * parties -> debtor -> customer_id - from Kafka topic EASYPAY-827 (customer_id)
 * signature_information - from Kafka topic EASYPAY-827

All other data - from pain.001

This data:
 * Ultimate debtor (with all data under it)
 * Charge bearer
 * Payment type information (with all data under it)

can be present in pain.001 twice.

Ultimate debtor (with all data under it) should be always taken according this logic:
 # From Credit transfer transaction information - if it exists there
 # If it does not exist in Credit transfer information - take it from Payment information

Payment type information (with all data under it) and Charge bearer should be always taken according this logic:
 # For not mass payments - from Credit transfer transaction information, if it exists there, otherwise, from Payment information
 # For mass payments - from Payment information, if it exists there, otherwise, from Credit transfer transaction information

 

If payment_file format is iso_v3, then convert creditor's address using such logic (from EASYPAY-255):
 * If no address line and no town are provided -> save all other provided address data to address line (concatenation rules below)
 * If no address line and no country are provided -> save all other provided address data to address line (concatenation rules below)

Concatenate address fields in this order:
 # Country
 # Country sub-division
 # Municipality
 # Town name
 # Town area
 # Post code
 # Post box
 # Street name
 # Building number
 # "-" Apartment number
 # Floor
 # House name
 # Department
 # Subdepartment

column1: [DB] Change GDW payment data loading interface
column47:
*Why:* to sent SEPA PAYMENT PARTY IDENTYRIER information in structured way to GDW
*When:* Text
*Where:* GDW loading interface
*What:* 

*Option A - Proposal for new  GDW Data Loading interface PAYMENTS.DW_PAYMENT_PARTY_IDENTIFIER.* 

As a primary enhancement to the Global Data Warehouse (GDW), I propose the creation of a dedicated data loading interface: PAYMENTS.DW_PAYMENT_PARTY_IDENTIFIER. This interface will be designed to load structured payment party identifier data separately. The loaded data can then be joined with the main payment data on the GDW side using GROUP_SIDs.

Importantly, the existing interface structure will be able to support historical data loading. This ensures backward compatibility and preserves access to legacy data without disruption as old fields would not be removed from existing data loading interface.

 

!https://wiki.swedbank.net/download/attachments/2179472257/image-2025-5-13_9-47-17.png?version=1&modificationDate=1747118837990&api=v2|width=800!

 

*Option B – Adjustments to Existing Data Loading Interface*

Option B must be considered, as the Global Data Warehouse (GDW) team is currently overloaded with ongoing activities and cannot implement the required changes for Option A on the GDW side.

As a result, we will need to proceed by modifying the business logic within the existing data loading interface, without altering its structure. This approach has been aligned with business stakeholders.

Per our agreement with business representatives, additional payment party identifiers will be ignored, as the system supports loading only one identifier per party. In scenarios where multiple identifiers exist for the same party, only one will be selected and forwarded to GDW based on predefined business rules and prioritization:
 * {*}Private Individuals{*}: NIDN → TXID → CUST → Date and Place of Birth → any other

 * {*}Organizations{*}: COID → LEI → TXID → BIC → any other

This ensures a consistent and prioritized approach to handling multiple identifiers while minimizing the need for structural changes

 

*!https://wiki.swedbank.net/download/attachments/2179472257/image-2025-5-13_9-50-39.png?version=1&modificationDate=1747119039000&api=v2|width=800!*

14.07.2025 15:33;p998osm;[~p998onx], [~p998gzv]
I see no benefit in filling new fields in the '..._PARTY_GROUP_SID' of the VMAKSKOR table. The VMAKSKOR table is already adapted for storing multiple ID values, which is currently used in international and SEPA cross-border payments. (In SEPA cross-border payments, one of the ID values is chosen based on a certain algorithm.) 

I propose eliminating additional steps:
Changes in filling the VMAKSKOR table (lt_vmk.lisa_valismakse): creation of entries with PAYMENT_PARTY_IDENTIFIER and their GROUP_SID entry into VMAKSKOR.
Changes in converting entries from the VMAKSKOR table to the VVMK structure (crebit.lt_vmk.vmakskor_to_vvmk): reading from PAYMENT_PARTY_IDENTIFIER and transforming into VVMK.
Changes in a view CORESRV.FOREIGN_OUTGOING_PMT_IN_BRANCH: fetch data from PAYMENT_PARTY_IDENTIFIER table

And keep only:
Changes in converting entries from the VVMK structure to DP, DP_ISO structure (payments.payment_utility.convert_vvmk_to_dp): adding entry creation with PAYMENT_PARTY_IDENTIFIER and their GROUP_SID entry into DP_ISO.

Furthermore, PAYMENT_PARTY_IDENTIFIER has an interface with DP/DP_ISO via the DP_ID field, and records of this table are archived together with DP/DP_ISO entries. Records from the VMAKSKOR table are archived after payment confirmation. There is uncertainty whether PAYMENT_PARTY_IDENTIFIER entries should be created only together with VMAKSKOR or separately with both VMAKSKOR and DP/DP_ISO. How archiving will proceed in each case?;;;

column1: LV STAR Domestic/European payment PDF (ID)
column47:
*Why:*  Identifications of Payer, Ultimate Payer, Beneficiary and Ultimate Beneficiary will be saved per new data model to support multiple IDs according to business rules.  Domestic/European payment PDFs must be adjusted to fetch data either per new or old data model. Fetching of data per old data model must be supported for historical payments.

*When:* Can be implemented at any time

*Where:* LV specific PDF for Domestic/European payments created in STAR from:
 * "Domestic payments" page after execution
 * "Print transactions" view form for Domestic/ European payment 
** Daily banking > Account activities > Print transactions | Domestic OUT
** Daily banking > Account activities > Print transactions | Domestic IN
** Daily banking > Account activities > Print transactions | Foreign/ EU OUT
* "Incoming international payments" view form
** Daily banking > Transactions > Incoming international payments | search and open payment, click on print button 
 
*What:* 
 # Outgoing/incoming payment | Payer/ Ultimate Payer/ Beneficiary/ Ultimate Beneficiary:
 ** ID data is fetched per old or new data model. 
 # Incoming payment | Payer/ Ultimate Payer:
 ** In case multiple occurrences of Organisation IDs are present for the same party, then only 1 ID is shown according to agreed priorities:
COID | LEI | TXID | BIC | any other

*Notes:* For new data model, see [Party identification mapping, priorities & examples.|https://wiki.swedbank.net/spaces/DPAY/pages/2273426761/Party+Identification]

column1: [DB] Change VAT rate for E-Invoice in crebit.vat_rules // Estonia
column47:
{*}Why{*}: Based on regulation: Value-Added Tax Act § 15 (1) Standard VAT rate changes from 22 % to 24 % in Estonia.

*When:* New standard VAT rate 24 % must be changed from {color:#ff8b00}*01.07.2025.*{color}

{*}Where{*}: Change must be done in core system set-up which generating VAT transaction.

*What:* New VAT Setup in the {{CREBIT.VAT_RULES}} Table
 *Create New Records:* Add new records in the {{crebit.vat_rules}} table for active {{op_id's}} with VAT rate of {*}24.00%{*}, starting from the date {*}01/07/2025{*}.
   (Note: Updates are not permitted, as historical information must be preserved and current setup must be active till end date)

 *Check VAT Applicable OP_ID Descriptions:* Review the descriptions for E-invoice VAT applicable op_id's. Ensure that *VAT rate information* is not included in the {{op_nimetus}} 
   and {{op_maksuaine}} fields. If VAT rate information is present, it must be updated accordingly.

 *Close Old Record:* Close the existing record with a {*}22.00% VAT rate{*}, ensuring the end date is set (currently it is null).

 *SQL query for VAT setup:* 
  {code:sql}
 select 
 v.op_id,
 v.vat_rate,
 v.vat_op_id,
 v.start_date,
 v.end_date,
 o.service_offering_id,
 o.op_nimetus,
 o.op_maksuaine
from 
 crebit.op_param o,
 crebit.vat_rules v 
where 
 o.service_offering_id = 'W712' and -- E-Invoice Baltic
 o.op_id = v.op_id and 
 v.vat_rate = '22.00' and
 (v.end_date > sysdate or v.end_date is null)
{code}
*Testing Steps:*
 # Verify that new E-invoice product-related records for VAT setup have been added to the {{crebit.vat_rule}} table.

 # Check if the {{crebit.op_param}} table does not contain any old VAT rates in the {{op_id}} descriptions, specifically for {{OP_NIMETUS}} and {{{}OP_MAKSUAINE{}}}.

column1: Validate pain.001 file content
column47:
*Why:* pain.001 has to be valid in order to execute payments in it
*When:* Text
*Where:* worker-payment-batch-handler
*What:*

If pain.001 is valid against XSD, then validate:
 * -validate if file name is not too long (?)-
 * check that file is not a duplicate (API EASYPAY-864 call) if duplicate, then reject file with error - see the table at the bottom
 * validate number of transactions in the file
 * validate total payments' amount in the file
 * validate that mass payment has only domestic payments in EUR (no other payment types)

 

Validate number of transactions in the file:
 # First validate whole number of transactions in the file
 ** from the file take value from <CstmrCdtTrfInitn><GrpHdr><NbOfTxs>
 ** calculate how many transactions (each transaction is in <CstmrCdtTrfInitn><PmtInf><CdtTrfTxInf>) are in the file
 ** compare if the numbers are the same
 # If validation is successful - proceed with next validations. If not - reject file with error - see the table at the bottom.

 

Validate total payments' amount in the file in the file:
 # First validate amount of all transactions in the file
 ** from the file take value from <CstmrCdtTrfInitn><GrpHdr><CtrlSum>
 ** calculate value of all transactions (each transaction is in <CstmrCdtTrfInitn><PmtInf><CdtTrfTxInf>) in the file
 ** compare if the numbers are the same
 # If validation is successful - proceed with next validations. If not - reject file with error - see the table at the bottom

 

Validate that mass payment has only domestic payments in EUR (no other payment types)
 # Validate all Payment information blocks - if any of them contains tag 'SALA' in <CstmrCdtTrfInitn><PmtInf><PmtTpInf><CtgyPurp><Cd> contains
 # If first validation finds payment information block. Check if there are any more payment information blocks in file
 ## If there are more than one payment information block - reject file (see error table)
 ## If that's the only payment information block - proceed with validation described below)

Precondition: tag <CstmrCdtTrfInitn><PmtInf><PmtTpInf><CtgyPurp><Cd> contains 'SALA'
 # Check that first two symbols of each creditor account (CstmrCdtTrfInitn><PmtInf><CdtTrfTxInf><CdtrAcct>) matches the first two symbols of debtor account (CstmrCdtTrfInitn><PmtInf><DbtrAcct>) and matches debtor country code (that is: all payments are domestic)
 # Check that currency (CstmrCdtTrfInitn><PmtInf><CdtTrfTxInf><InstdAmt Ccy="EUR">) is EUR for all transactions
 # If both validations are successful - proceed with updating file status to Validated. If not - reject file with error - see the table at the bottom

 

 

If validation passes, then call API PAYME-1039 with values:
 * File SID - from registration
 * Status - VALIDATED
 * Format - from file
 * Total amount - from file
 * Total number of transactions - from file
 * Original Message Identification - from file

If validation fails, then call API PAYME-1039 with values:
 * File SID - from registration
 * Status - REJECTED
 * Format - from file
 * Error code - from validation, provide SID

 

Error codes
|SID|Error code in xml|Error description|
|ERR00001|DUPLICATION|Duplicate file|
|ERR00002| |Number of transactions in the file does not match with transactions count in the file|
|ERR00003|INVALID_CONTROL_SUM|Amounts of transactions in the file do not match control sum of the file|
|ERR00004|INVALID_DATA|Mass payment contains international payments|
|ERR00005|FILE_PARSING_ERROR|General error - if not other error found|

column1: Kafka connection failed - EHI for W981 service
column47:
Service Offering ID: W981

Service Offering Name: Baltic Payment event streaming.

Dispatcher:  *_No_*

On-Call: *_No_*

 

*Operations Center Action:*

When event appears the Baltic Payment Data is not set to Kafka Enterprise Platform.

{*}Operations Center action{*}: to send the event as an incident in *SNAP to ‘Baltic Payments’* assignment group during Baltic workdays 08:00-17:00 EET and all other time.

*Operations Center should not call* 'Baltic Payments' On-Call team at any time as service criticality class do not requires instant fix.

 

*Event Description:* 

Event Handling instruction is created to prevent payment data losses in the Kafka Enterprise Platform (Payment Baltic raw topic). Payment data loss can occur for various reasons, which the most common being a lost connection to the Kafka platform, among others, which could result that BpayStream application receiving information from AQ but being unable to push it to Kafka. In such case, the application should attempt to resend messages to Kafka as many times as it is specified in the repeater parameter. If the messages still fail to send, then the BpayStream application must redirect messages to the "Dead Letter Queue" for manual reprocessing.

When such a situation happens BpayStram application must trigger Swedbank Alert System according to described monitoring rules in Prometheus. For this particular case Payments Baltic maintenance employee must check if Kafka connection is restored and if it is then payment messages must be restored/moved from "Dead Letter Queue" to main AQ, which is listened by BpayStream application.

 

*Additional Information:* testing by QA & maintenance

column1: Create STREAM bpay_fraud_monitoring_stream
column47:
In order to move selected information (payments) from our Raw topic to Fraud Monitoring Topic we should use ksqlDB tool which is provided by our vendor Confluence. ksqlDB allows us to query our Row topic and move selected data to preferable location. In ksqlDB, we select and store data in a streams, which must have strongly defined data schema.

code for STREAM creation:
{code:sql}
  CREATE OR REPLACE STREAM bpay_fraud_monitoring_stream WITH (KAFKA_TOPIC='W981.baltic.payments.fraud.monitoring.topic', VALUE_FORMAT='AVRO', VALUE_AVRO_SCHEMA_FULL_NAME='W981.baltic.payments.raw.topic-value')
    AS
    SELECT
     paymentId, 
     debtorAccountNumber,
     creditorAccountNumber,
     amount,
     currency,
     details,
     creditorReferenceNumber,
     ...
    FROM W981.baltic.payments.raw.topic
    WHERE status IN ('C', 'N', 'R') AND holderChannelCode IN ('PKM', 'SOP')
    EMIT CHANGES;
{code}
More information about ksqlDB STREAMS can be found hear:
[https://www.confluent.io/blog/how-real-time-stream-processing-works-with-ksqldb/?_ga=2.46309935.906919299.1729078839-1420397618.1729078839]

Used commands for DB manipulation:

Guide of field updates:

Identify Missing Fields & Data Sources
Before making updates, I identified which fields were missing or incorrectly mapped in crebit.dp_iso.
Key sources of required data:

crebit.dp (main payment storage)
crebit.dp_iso (PDF-relevant data)
payments.payment_party_identifier (beneficiary party details)
payments.iso_post_address (addresses linked to payments)
payments.iso_agent (bank-related information)
Update Beneficiary Bank Details
I updated Beneficiary Bank Name, BIC in crebit.dp_iso from payments.iso_agent.

SQL: Fetch & Update Beneficiary Bank Name & BIC

UPDATE crebit.dp_iso i
SET 
    i.creditor_lei = (
        SELECT a.name FROM payments.iso_agent a
        WHERE a.sid = (SELECT d.creditor_agent_sid FROM crebit.dp d WHERE d.id = i.dp_id)
    ),
    i.creditor_address_1 = (
        SELECT a.bic FROM payments.iso_agent a
        WHERE a.sid = (SELECT d.creditor_agent_sid FROM crebit.dp d WHERE d.id = i.dp_id)
    )
WHERE i.dp_id = 2309621755;
COMMIT;
Update Beneficiary (Final Receiver) Name
I extracted the final beneficiary's name from payments.payment_party_identifier and stored it in crebit.dp_iso.

SQL: Fetch & Store Beneficiary Name

UPDATE crebit.dp_iso i
SET 
    i.ult_creditor_name = (
        SELECT p.party_id 
        FROM payments.payment_party_identifier p 
        WHERE p.dp_id = i.dp_id
        FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY
    )
WHERE i.dp_id = 2309621755;
COMMIT;
Update Beneficiary Residency Status
Logic:

If creditor_res_country is "LV", set "Resident"
Otherwise, set "Non-Resident"
SQL: Update Residency Status

UPDATE crebit.dp_iso
SET creditor_reference_issuer = 
    CASE 
        WHEN creditor_res_country = 'LV' THEN 'Resident'
        ELSE 'Non-Resident'
    END
WHERE dp_id = 2309621755;
COMMIT;
Update Beneficiary Country
I fetched Beneficiary’s Country from payments.payment_party_identifier.birth_country.

SQL: Fetch & Update Beneficiary Country

UPDATE crebit.dp_iso
SET ult_creditor_address_country = (
    SELECT birth_country FROM payments.payment_party_identifier
    WHERE dp_id = 2309621755
    FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY
);
COMMIT;
Update Beneficiary Address (Street, City, Country)
Step 1: Insert missing address in payments.iso_post_address

INSERT INTO payments.iso_post_address (sid, address_line1, address_line2, country_code)
VALUES (
    (SELECT group_sid FROM payments.payment_party_identifier WHERE dp_id = 2309621755 FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY),
    'Beneficiary Street 123',  
    'Tallinn',                  
    'EE'                        
);
COMMIT;
Step 2: Update crebit.dp_iso with correct address details

UPDATE crebit.dp_iso i
SET 
    i.ult_creditor_address_1 = (
        SELECT pa.address_line1 
        FROM payments.iso_post_address pa
        WHERE pa.sid = (
            SELECT p.group_sid 
            FROM payments.payment_party_identifier p 
            WHERE p.dp_id = i.dp_id
            FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY
        )
    ),
    i.ult_creditor_address_2 = (
        SELECT pa.address_line2 || ', ' || pa.country_code 
        FROM payments.iso_post_address pa
        WHERE pa.sid = (
            SELECT p.group_sid 
            FROM payments.payment_party_identifier p 
            WHERE p.dp_id = i.dp_id
            FETCH FIRST 1 ROWS ONLY
        )
    )
WHERE i.dp_id = 2309621755;
COMMIT;
 Final Verification & Data Sync
After all updates, I validated if the fields in crebit.dp_iso were correctly filled.

SQL: Verify Updates

SELECT dp_id, 
       ult_creditor_name AS Beneficiary_Name,
       ult_creditor_address_1 AS Beneficiary_Street, 
       ult_creditor_address_2 AS Beneficiary_City_Country, 
       ult_creditor_address_country AS Beneficiary_Country,
       creditor_reference_issuer AS Resident_Status
FROM crebit.dp_iso

column1: Create alert in Swedbank Alerts system
column47:
An alert is necessary to prevent payment data losses in the Kafka Enterprise Platform (Payment Baltic raw topic). The most common incident leading to data loss is a disconnection from the Kafka platform. If the BpayStream app cannot send messages to Kafka, it must create an alert in the Swedbank Alerts system ([https://alerts.swedbank.net/alerts]).
This can be accomplished from the Andromeda platform by creating a new Prometheus monitoring rule and using API.
For more detailed information, please refer to the link [https://spacetime.swedbank.net/reference-docs/observability/alerts].

Alert information:
Event Handling Instruction - KB0033379
Resource – BpayStream
Message – Connection to Kafka is lost.
Event – Payment message sent to Kafka.

{*}Testing Notes{*}: tested with EASYPAY-776.

column1: [TESTING] Check  "Dead Letter Queue" functionality for BpayStream app
column47:
*Why:* 
To prevent payment data losses in the Kafka Enterprise Platform (Payment Baltic raw topic)
*When:* 
No particular date;
*Where:* 
BpayStream integration application
*What:*
An error handling process is necessary to prevent payment data losses in the Kafka Enterprise Platform (Payment Baltic raw topic). Payment data loss can occur for various reasons, which the most common being a lost connection to the Kafka platform, among others, which could result that BpayStream application receiving information from AQ but being unable to push it to Kafka. In such case, the application should attempt to resend messages to Kafka as many times as it is specified in the repeater parameter. If the messages still fail to send, then the BpayStream application must redirect those messages to the "Dead Letter Queue" for manual reprocessing.

*Additional information:*
*What is a dead-letter queue?*
A dead-letter queue (DLQ) is a special type of message queue that temporarily stores messages that a software system cannot process due to errors. Message queues are software components that support asynchronous communication in a distributed system. They let you send messages between software services at any volume and don’t require the message receiver to always be available. A dead-letter queue specifically stores erroneous messages that have no destination or which can’t be processed by the intended receiver.

Dead-letter queues (DLQ) exist alongside regular message queues. They act as temporary storage for erroneous and failed messages. DLQs prevent the source queue from overflowing with unprocessed messages.

For example, consider a software that has a regular message queue and a DLQ. The software uses the regular queue to hold messages it plans to send to a destination. If the receiver fails to respond or process the sent messages, the software moves them to the dead-letter queue.

There are two potential causes when messages move to the DLQ pipeline: erroneous message content and changes in the receiver’s system.
*Translation labels (if any):* 
N/A
*Possible impacts (changes could impact other applications/ processes etc.):*
N/A
*Acceptance criteria/ testing notes:*
1. Process a domestic payment.
2. Verify if the payment is in the final status; crebit.dp.status should be 'C', 'N', or 'R'.
3. Confirm that payment data has been entered into the new AQ.
4. Disconnect the BpayStream application from the Kafka Enterprise Platform.
5. Launch the BpayStream application.
6. After a few minutes, check the main AQ to ensure the payment/message has been cleared from the main AQ and it is now in the "Dead Letter" AQ.

column1: [DB] Create procedure for Data restoring from dead letter queue to main AQ
column47:
*Why:* 
To prevent payment data losses in the Kafka Enterprise Platform (Payment Baltic raw topic)
*When:* 
No particular date;
*Where:* 
DB procedure;
*What:*

When the connection to the Kafka platform is lost, the BpayStream application will continue to receive information from AQ but will be unable to push it to Kafka. In such cases, the application will attempt to resend the messages to Kafka, based on the number of retries specified in the "repeater" parameter. If the messages fail to send after the specified number of attempts, the BpayStream application will redirect those messages to the "Dead Letter Queue."

Once the connection to the Kafka platform is restored, all messages in the "Dead Letter Queue" must be resent to the main AQ. To to this, we require a database procedure to restore these messages.

column639:
13.12.2024 12:26;p998osm;Done:
 * For SEPA payments in D status (faulty incoming payments) Return debit transaction (dprw) is created in vm.korresp_toiming table with value date = greatest of banking day and settlement day. For Return with settlement date bigger than current date values of fields crebit.dp.value_date and crebit.dp.earliest_credit_time are recalculated - greatest of calculated current value and settlement day is taken.
 * For SEPApayments in C status there are no changes - Return debit transaction is created in position_keeping.transaction with value date of current day. The same values stay for value_date and earliest_credit_time.
 * For all outgoing Returns (SEPA, Instant) crebit.dp.origin_bank_txid field value is constructed from debit transaction date and number (either vm.korresp_toiming.op_nr either crebit.dp.remit_trn_id - it depends where debit transaction has been made- in vm.korresp_toiming or position_keeping.transaction ) and later is taken by application for RtrId value.
 * All automatic SEPA Returns are put into queue by DB procedure.
 * All SEPA Returns are put into queue with delay in case settlement day is bigger than banking day.

As there is might be time interval between Releasing of DB changes and Sepa-exchange, debit transaction part is under sysglobal RETURN_DB_TRNS_NEW. While it's value is N, debit transaction will be created in old way - position_keeping.transactions. So after release value of RETURN_DB_TRNS_NEW has to be changed to Y. It can be done by maintenance at day time.

 

For QA:
 * Sysglobal RETURN_DB_TRNS_NEW value is N. Create incoming payments:

 # Sepa with settlement date the same as current date

 # Instant OK
 # Instant NOT OK (Reject will be sent)

 * For created payments except 5, 6, 8 create Return in Forms Teller
 * Repeat the same steps when value of sysglobal RETURN_DB_TRNS_NEW is changed to Y.

 * To check financial reports (next 1-2 days)

 * "st2": STEP2 flow only
 * "rt1": RT1 flow only

sepa-web stays common and shall be deployed with SEPA instances only.

column1: RT1: Business date in TIPS camt.054 message
column47:
*Why:* The camt.054.001.06 message is used in TIPS to report the account owner about the successful execution of either a debited or credited liquidity transfer.
The message specification of camt.054 message reports the booking date and time in the field BkToCstmrDbtCdtNtfctn/Ntfctn/Ntry/BookgDt/DtTm; i.e. the timestamp including the calendar date of the settlement of the liquidity transfer on the TIPS DCA.
The booking date and the business date in TIPS do not match after TIPS opens the new business date. This leads to errors in the internal reconciliation of banks.
TIPS will introduce in Nov.2024 release a change by introducing the value date into the camt.054 in the following field: BkToCstmrDbtCdtNtfctn/Ntfctn/Ntry/ValDt.

*When:* From Nov.2024 release ({*}RT1 release date & time:{*} {color:#de350b}*November 17th 2024*{color} between 00:30 and 03:30 CET)

*! EBA test period:* September 24th - October 31st 2024. *Self-Certification deadline: {color:#de350b}October 31st 2024.{color}*

*Where:*
 * ISO exchange
 * PAYMENTS_ISO.DEBT_CRED_NOTIFICATION table

*What:*
1. System books transactions according to camt.054 XML from TIPS and RT1, with
value date = BkToCstmrDbtCdtNtfctn/Ntfctn/Ntry/ValDt (i.e. TIPS Business Date in which the liquidity transfer settlement took place).
{panel}
 * PAYMENTS_ISO.DEBT_CRED_NOTIFICATION - Check that value date is stored according to value from XML.
 ** VALUE_DATE = BkToCstmrDbtCdtNtfctn/Ntfctn/Ntry/ValDt value date from XML
 * VM.KORRESP_TOIMING - Check with both, current value date and past value date.
 ** TEGELIK_VAARTUSPAEV = PAYMENTS_ISO.DEBT_CRED_NOTIFICATION.VALUE_DATE
 ** VAARTUSPAEV = DEBT_CRED_NOTIFICATION.VALUE_DATE or system date, when value date in past{panel}
2. DB field PAYMENTS_ISO.DEBT_CRED_NOTIFICATION.VALUE_DATE comment is updated to remove remark "(not present in TIPS)".
----
*Comments:*
 * camt.054 processing rules are defined in PAYMENTS_ISO.DEBT_CRED_NOTIFICATION_RULES with INT_SERVICE_CODE = 'TIPS', 'RT1'
 * If transaction is required, its registered in PAYMENTS_ISO.DEBT_CRED_NOTIFICATION and then booked to system.
 * EBA sample files: [^IPSPSP.CAMT054.EBA_IPS-2024-08-06_16-18.XML], [^IPSPSP.CAMT054.EBA_IPS-2024-08-07_10_04_27.340.xml]
 * Message received in PPTE: [^camt.054-test.xml]
 * TIPS camt.054 XML: See PAYRUN-1646

column47:
*Why:*  Payments between resident and non-resident >= 10000 EUR (IDENT_MRES_LIMIIT ) should be included in LV CB NAMP report which takes payments from CREBIT.TOIM_CB.

*When:* Any time before SEPA_FLOW_MERGE_START.

*Where:* coresrv.dp_out_trn.credit (SEPA), payments.transactions_pkg.credit (instant)

*What:* Information about credited incoming payment (any out_channel_code) should be saved to CREBIT.TOIM_CB if
 * payment is between resident and non-resident AND
 * amount is >= IDENT_MRES_LIMIIT

Payment is between resident and non-resident in following cases:
 * substr(DEBTOR_AGENT_BIC, 5, 2) is not 'LV' AND beneficiary is resident
 * substr(DEBTOR_AGENT_BIC, 5, 2) is 'LV' AND beneficiary is non-resident

Beneficiary residence should be derived from customer data. 

*Acceptance criteria:* 

Incoming instant and SEPA payments (SEPI, SEPCI, SEPGI, SIPI, EKSI, EKSCI) are saved in CREBIT.TOIM_CB as follows:
|*AC #*|*Amount*|*Payer’s residency*
*(debtor agent BIC)*|*Beneficiary’s residency*
*(customer data)*|*Should be saved* 
*to TOIM_CB?*|
|1|< 10000|any|any|No|
|2|>= 10000|LV|LV|No|
|3|>= 10000|not LV|not LV|No|
|4|>= 10000|LV|not LV|Yes|
|5|>= 10000|not LV|LV|Yes|

 

*Comments:* In current SEPA DP, only instant payments (SIPI) are saved to crebit.toim_cb (implemented with FPAY-29). SEPCO, SEPGO, EKSCO won't be saved without development. As also instant payments saving is not implemented accordingly to business requirements (see attached email) then we lets fix it also with this task.

column47:
*WHY:*  From SEPA Flow Merge, cross-border and intragroup SEPA payments will appear in DP.  Such payments should be included in daily report of the teller that inserted the payment in STAR.

*WHEN:* Latest by date specified in SEPA_FLOW_MERGE_START (can be done earlier since payments with such out_channel_code cannot appear before FM start)

*WHERE:* STAR: Administrative -> Teller daily reports -> Daily reports (payments) (administrative/teller-daily-reports/daily-reports-payments-new) 

*WHAT:* 
 * Payments with dp.out_channel_code in ('SEPCO', 'SEPGO', 'EKSCO') should be included under section \{*}'Foreign payment orders'{*}. Proposed mapping:
 ** Remitter account:  DP.DEBTOR_ACC_NUMBER
 ** Beneficiary account: DP.CREDITOR_ACC_NUMBER
 ** Amount: DP.AMOUNT
 ** Currency: DP.CURRENCY
 ** ID: DP.ID
 ** Branch: DP.BRANCH_CODE
 * Payments with dp.out_channel_code in ('SEPCO', 'SEPGO', 'EKSCO') should not be included under 'Payment orders below customer double identification limit'

 

*Comments:*

This report contains all payments (except cancelled) inserted by teller on current date. SEPA cross-border payments will not go via double identification process (crebit.dp_out_acceptance) but will be accepted as foreign payments (crebit.vmakskor) and after acceptance stored in crebit.DP. As SEPA cross-border payments are "foreign payment orders" from teller/customer perspective then these must be presented as "Foreign payment orders".

column1: PB Implement automated Standing Order Agreement closure if agreement was not activated during 7 calendar days
column47:
*Why:*
 * According to GDPR (TIDY program) requirements aligned with PB lawyers it must be implemented data retention/ destruction rules for Standing Order Agreements if agreement was not activated during 1 year:
 ** [SEPA Payments Baltic TIDY application assessment.|https://workspaces.swedbank.net/sites/TIDY/Shared%20Documents/DB%26IT/BB%20Consumer%20Payments/Approved/SEPA%20Payments%20Baltic%20TIDY%20Application%20assessment%20template_1.5_2022xlsx.xlsx?d=wc0b86e7eed6d41eba4429578d8077886]
 ** [International payments TIDY application assessment|https://workspaces.swedbank.net/sites/TIDY/Shared%20Documents/DB%26IT/BB%20Consumer%20Payments/Approved/International%20Payments%20TIDY%20Application%20assessment%20template_1.5_2022xlsx.xlsx?d=w75c68dc83d664f4e8da1cc8a2084bd62].
 ** [Summary of Baltic Payments area products data retention/ deletion rules.|https://wiki.swedbank.net/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=2030189620#expand-SummaryofBalticPaymentsareaproductsdataretentiondeletionrules]
 * Business representatives have decided that it is more efficient to have implement *automated process* for such agreements with status 'O' (Waiting for authorisation) tracking and closure.
 * It is planned to send Standing Order agreements data to MDM AgrSum for global data disposal orchestration. From MDM Agreement Summary side it will be tracked status change from ’O’ (Waiting for authorisation) ->’M’(Inactive) and it will be possible to apply different data retention calculation and retention rule than for generally applied rule when agreement status is changed from 'A' (authorised/active) to ’M’(Inactive) .
 * With product business representative agreed that Standing Order agreements with status 'O' (Waiting for authorisation) should be terminated after 7 days, then from GDM AgrSum side this agreement data will be deleted after 358 days (in total after 12 months after record creation).    
 * It is planned to send agreement's data to MDM Agreement summary all non-closed agreements including the ones created earlier than 2007.01.01 and all active and closed agreements which are closed >= 01.01.2007.
 * According to test database currently there are EE: 4, LT: 17, LV: 1 standing order agreements with status ’O’ (Waiting for authorization) that were created more than 1 year ago.

*When:* Until implementation of Agreement summary integration.

*Where:* In PB Core database table crebit.per_mk.

*What:*

1. PB:  implement automated Standing Standing Order Agreement closure process for agreements that were created {*}more than 7 days ago{*}:
 * 
 ** Change status: ’O’ (Waiting for authorisation) ->’M’(Inactive); 
 ** Frequency of automated process running: daily. 

2. PB: it should be also changed for currently existing records EE: 4, LT: 17, LV: 1 standing order agreements with status ’O’ (Waiting for authorization) status to 'M' (inactive).

*Possible impacts (changes could impact other applications/ processes etc.):* 

*Acceptance criteria/ testing notes:* 
 # Run automated process and test in db if standing order agreements with status 'O' that were created more than 7 days ago status was changed to 'M'.
 # Check if it was changed status to 'M' for old agreement records EE: 4, LT: 17, LV: 1.

column1: (SEPA-Exchange) Receive proprietary status report from ProSwitch
column47:
*WHY:* Intragroup messages sent to ProSwitch receive the status report (ACK/NACK) in proprietary ProSwitch format, not in standard ISO pacs.002 format. Message status should be updated according to the status report.

*WHERE:* In SEPA-Exchange, when proprietary status report (only ProSwitch header, no message body) has been received in incoming queue from ProSwitch.

*WHEN:* After date & time defined with sysglobal SEPA_FLOW_MERGE_START. Before that date & time intragroup messages must be processed by SEPA-Transfer, still.

*WHAT:* 
 # Listen and receive messages from the existing incoming queue used by SEPA-Transfer today
 # Parse the header and read
 ## the our/bank reference from the APPLICATION KEY field '015'
 ## the return code from the RETURN CODE field '016'
 # Find the sent message by our/bank reference (vm.sepa_document.local_bank_trans_id) and update its status (vm.sepa_document.status_code) to
 ## 'A - accepted' in case of return code 'OK'
 ## 'N - not accepted' in case of return code other than 'OK' with return code saved as error code (vm.sepa_document.error_code)

*Acceptance criteria:*

*WHY:* It is needed to return credited intragroup payment either by request of customer or after receiving recall.

Additionally, with outgoing intragroup return messages it is needed to :
 # Intragroup return payments must follow different cut-off time ([https://jira.swedbank.net/browse/PAYRUN-1285]) than defined for domestic and cross-border SEPA return payments and stop the return payment (holder_channel >> 'CUT') in case sending after cut-off is not allowed
 # Assign new processing flow code 'GF'
(in crebit.dp_sepa.create_return procedure, called by SEPA-Exchange)
 # Wrap messages into the proprietary ProSwitch header as done currently in SEPA-Transfer
 # Send messages to ProSwitch by putting them to the existing outgoing queue used by SEPA-Transfer
 # Set message straight to final status after processing the response from ProSwitch. 2nd response from EBA is not expected in this flow:
 ## in case of positive response: initial status 'S - Sent' becomes 'A - Accepted', there is no intermediary status 'B - In Bulker' used
 ## in case of error: S > E ? (check how it is done in SEPA-Transfer today)
 ## in case of negative response: S > N ? (check how it is done in SEPA-Transfer today)

2. Created return payment is stored with DP.OUT_CHANNEL_CODE = 'SEPGO'

3. System creates and stores pacs.004.001.09 RETURN message data and routes message to ProSwitch using intragroup flow (GF).

5. System processes ProSwitch response of message acceptance or non-acceptance and sets the message to final status

6. User can find outgoing SEPGO return payment via outgoing payment search.

column1: (SEPA-Exchange) Receive pacs.004.001.09 (RETURN) for intragroup payment (FOCR + ordinary return)
column47:
*WHY:* To process incoming intragroup payment returns as 
 * to credit incoming return to customer account automatically if return reason is not "FOCR"
 * to credit incoming return manually if return reason is "FOCR".

*WHERE:* In SEPA-Exchange, when intragroup payment return message (pacs.004.001.09) has been received in incoming queue from ProSwitch.

*WHEN:* After date & time defined with sysglobal SEPA_FLOW_MERGE_START. Before that date & time intragroup messages must be processed by SEPA-Transfer, still.

*WHAT:* 
 # Listen and receive messages from the existing incoming queue used by SEPA-Transfer today
 # Unwrap messages from the proprietary ProSwitch header and process messages as usual
 # Related outgoing intragroup SCT should already be findable via vm.sepa_cdm_api.get_ret_orig_doc_id procedure.
 # Assign processing flow code 'GF' to intragroup messages
 # Calculate correct out channel code according to payment data, cannot assign 'SEPGI' automatically, since there can also appear old x-border (non-intragroup) payments which were held in Proscan during the flow merge go-live!

 

*Acceptance criteria:*

1.  System processes and stores incoming pacs.004.001.09 RETURN message received from ProSwitch using processing_flow_code='GF', relates message to outgoing intragroup SCT and creates incoming return payment in DP with following out_channel_code:
 * Intragroup return - SEPGI
 * Cross-border return - SEPCI (in case of old cross-border payment)

2. User can find incoming SEPGI return payment via incoming payment search.

3. User can see received RETURN message in Forms Teller via "SEPA case details", "SEPA message chain" forms.

4. User can view pacs.004 message complete data by clicking [Message details] in “SEPA message chain" or "SEPA case details" form.

5. When there is no related outgoing case then return payment is credited to customer account automatically. 

6. When there exists related outgoing case then return payment is set as faulty and needs to be processed manually via case.

7. Funds are credited to customer with op_id
 * Intragroup return - '7RG'
 * Cross-border return - '7RC'

8. Nostro transactions are done to SEPA1EUR {color:#172b4d}using domestic transaction types (dpic - Incoming domestic payment to corr.account){color}

*Comments:*
 * {color:#172b4d}For defining out_channel_code:{color}
 ** Domestic SEPA payment = debtor agent BIC country is local country
 ** Cross-border SEPA payment = debtor agent BIC country is not local country and debtor agent BIC is not intragroup BIC.
 ** Intragroup SEPA payment = debtor agent BIC is intragroup BIC (HG_SWIFT_LIST)

column1: Error when processing SEB answer to pacs.028.001.01
column47:
Instant payment is sent to beneficiary bank, we receive accept successfully. And after accept, payment is in final status (example id=1920565958). After we sent recall, we didn't  received answer and back office sent status update messages and we receive answer to status update messages with incorrect message status from SEB. Like for example:

CT                  O    P       2023-02-08 14:03:41 pacs.008.001.02

ACCEPT           I    P        2023-02-08 14:03:42 pacs.002.001.03

RECALL          O    P       2023-02-08 16:32:53 CAMT.056.001.01

ST_UPDATE    O    P       2023-02-24 10:02:04 pacs.028.001.01
ST_UPDATE    O    P       2023-03-02 14:55:11 pacs.028.001.01

So, after sent pacs.028.001.01 we receive answer from SEB with pacs.002.001.03 and reason 'RJCT' which we cannot perform and this happens every day. Payment is archived and sepa manual message reason after receiving incorrect message is 'paymentDoesNotExist' .Attaching pacs.002.001.03 from SEB after our sent ST_UPDATE.

So I can see few ways how to deal with it:
1. No changes from development. These messages go to manual processing and maintenance getting alerts .
2. We add searching in dp_arh table on application side. If it will help (will not get new type of errors) then these messages will be proccessed and data will go to vm.sepa_... tables. But we don't get any benefit of it.
3. We skip processing of pacs.002 when it is reply to pacs.0028.;;;

|CREATED_BY|VARCHAR2(30)|Record created by whom (Username)|
|CREATED_DTIME|DATE| |
|LAST_MODIFIED_BY|VARCHAR2(30)| |
|LAST_MODIFIED_DTIME|DATE| |
|SID|NUMBER(11)| |
|DEPARTMENT|VARCHAR2(70)|Department <Dept> - Identification of a division of a large organisation or building.|
|SUB_DEPARTMENT|VARCHAR2(70)|SubDepartment <SubDept> - Identification of a sub-division of a large organisation or building.|

column1: [DB] New DB attributes for SEPA message storing
column47:
With SEPA Rulbook 2023 changes all versions of receiving/ sending messages will be increased as well. Higher message versions include some fields which was not used. Therefore, we need to create new DB attributes to be able to store new message information and later on pass it for processing.

New information mainly related to SEPA post address (separate task), LEI – legal entity identification and account proxy information and couple fields are added to SEPA return message.

Full structure of new fields can be found in Projects.Ongoing projects.SEPA Rulebook 2023.Data management.Physical Data View.New DB attributes for SEPA message soring
 
|*VM.SEPA_CREDIT_TRANSFER*| | |
|ULT_CREDITOR_ORG_LEI|VARCHAR2(20)|Ultimate Creditor legal entity Identifier of the financial institution <CdtTrfTxInf><UltmtCdtr><Id><OrgId><LEI>|
|ULT_DEBTOR_ORG_LEI|VARCHAR2(20)|Ultimate Debtor legal entity Identifier of the financial institution  <CdtTrfTxInf><UltmtDbtr><Id><OrgId><LEI>|
|CREDITOR_POST_ADR_SID|NUMBER(8)|Creditor address identifier from VM.SEPA_POST_ADDRESS.SID|
|CREDITOR_ORG_LEI|NUMBER(20)|Creditor legal entity Identifier of the financial institution  <CdtTrfTxInf><Dbtr><Id><OrgId><LEI>|
|CREDITOR_ACCOUNT_PROXY_CODE|VARCHAR2(4)|The Creditor Account Proxy code <CdtTrfTxInf><CdtrAcct><Prxy><Tp><Cd>|
|CREDITOR_ACCOUNT_PROXY_PRTRY|VARCHAR2(35)|The Creditor Account Proxy Proprietary <CdtTrfTxInf><CdtrAcct><Prxy><Tp><Prtry>|
|CREDITOR_ACCOUNT_PROXY_ID|VARCHAR2(320)|The Creditor Account Proxy Id. <CdtTrfTxInf><CrdtAcct><Prxy><Id>|
|DEBTOR_ORG_LEI|NUMBER(20)|Debtor legal entity Identifier of the financial institution  <CdtTrfTxInf><Cdtr><Id><OrgId><LEI>|
|DEBTOR_POST_ADR_SID|NUMBER(8)|Debtor address identifier from VM.SEPA_POST_ADDRESS.SID|
|DEBTOR_ACCOUNT_PROXY_CODE|VARCHAR2(4)|The Debtor Account Proxy code <CdtTrfTxInf><DbtrAcct><Prxy><Tp><Cd>|
|DEBTOR_ACCOUNT_PROXY_PRTRY|VARCHAR2(35)|The Debtor Account Proxy Proprietary <CdtTrfTxInf><DbtrAcct><Prxy><Tp><Prtry>|
|DEBTOR_ACCOUNT_PROXY_ID|VARCHAR2(320)|The Debtor Account Proxy Id. <CdtTrfTxInf><DbtrAcct><Prxy><Id>|
|CLEARING_SYSTEM_CODE|VARCHAR2(4)| |

 
|*VM.SEPA_RETURN_ORIG*| | |
|PURPOSE_CODE|VARCHAR2(4)|Original transaction purpose code <Document><PmtRtr><TxInf><OrgnlTxRef><Purp><Cd>|

column1: The view crebit.pfs_taf doesn't work correctly for FEB months, except league year ( when exists FEB 29th)
column47:
*The problem:*

We have INC05250659: 

Client name, reg.nr. or a/a. or code: 
    LT057300010154262461
Description: 
    Please clarify why the group account annual fee from the account LT057300010154262461 was debited twice - 
3.02.2023 and 3.03.2023
2023020300104594   TT | Grupes saskaitos metinis mokestis 2023.01 | 202,73;
2023030300090672      TT | Grupes saskaitos metinis mokestis 2023.02 |202,73.

Trust account LT737300090154262591 was created at 29-01-2018

*Investigation :*

Trust annual fee (operation id 99KA) for group accounts works monthly , on day the 3th, via ROOBERT, crebit.pf_entry.id =9

view crebit. pfs_taf:

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW CREBIT.PFS_TAF AS
SELECT p.ID pf_id
     , p.period_to pf_period_to
     , a.anr base_id
     , a.anr cp_acc_no
     , NULL cp_acc_type
     , NULL cp_acc_subtype
     , NULL cp_acc_pricelist
     , NULL cp_cust_type
     , NULL cp_boc
     , NULL cp_amount
     , crebit.sysconst.get_local_currency cp_ccy
     , p.op_id cp_fee_id
     , NULL cp_fee_type
     , NULL cp_benef_bank
     , NULL cp_benef_acc
     , 'Y' cp_sp_enabled
     , 'N' cp_lp_style_fee
     , p.period_to cp_fee_validation_date
     , leia_tt_anr(a.anr, a.aliik, a.alamliik) op_acc_no
     , crebit.sysconst.get_local_currency op_ccy
     , SUBSTR(o.op_maksuaine || ' ' || TO_CHAR(p.period_to, 'YYYY.MM'), 1, 140) op_info
     , p.op_id op_id
     , p.run_date + p.pmt_delta + ROUND((MOD(ROWNUM / 100000, p.pmt_diffusion)), 0) wef
     , 'C' effective
     , NULL op_amt
     , p.option_convert op_option_convert
     , p.option_fdebit op_option_fdebit
     , p.option_reserve op_option_reserve
     , p.cost_unit op_cost_unit
     , p.orig_code op_orig_code
     , p.option_group option_group
     , a.anr product_id
  FROM crebit.valarve a
     , crebit.op_param o
     , crebit.pf p
 WHERE a.aliik = 'K'   -- trust account
   AND a.teen_anr IS NOT NULL   -- if teen_anr is null, then service fee unable to withdraw
   AND a.akuup <= ADD_MONTHS(p.period_to, -12)   -- 1 year or more old
   AND MOD(MONTHS_BETWEEN(p.period_to, a.akuup), 12) < 1
   AND a.olek IN('2', '3')   -- blocked or active
   AND p.op_id = o.op_id
   AND p.ID = '9'   -- trust annual fee
;

I checked concrete example:

select MOD(MONTHS_BETWEEN('28-feb-2023','29-jan-2018'), 12) from dual gives result 0.967741935483871 and it is <1

*Conclusion:*

The view crebit.pfs_taf doesn't work correctly for FEB months, except league year ( when exists FEB 29th)

Example select MOD(MONTHS_BETWEEN('29-feb-2024','29-jan-2018'), 12) from dual gives result 1.

*TO BE:*

Fix the view crebit. pfs_taf so that there will not be taken annul fee  on March for group accounts what is created on January.

column1: Using TLS for SEPA-Exchange connection to MQ
column47:
Secure connection using TLS must be established between SEPA-Exchange and MQ servers.

Recommended steps:

1. Order a new channels from MQ team

-every application should use its own MQ channels.
-separate channels have to be used for every MQ manager for every environment (test, gate, prod) and country
-estimate needed connection number for every new channel
-list MQ queues to be accessed by newly ordered channels

2. Adapt application for using TLS connection

3. Order TLS certificates to be used for connection and send info to MQ team

4. Switch application to  the new TLS MQ channels

5. Inform MQ team for deleting not used old MQ channels

 

New channels (xx indicates a country code):
||MQ channel||Connections||Environment||
|MQCQ.TO.SEPAX.xx.001|?|PROD|
|MQTQ.TO.SEPAX.xx.001|?|TEST|
|MQTQ.TO.SEPAX.xx.002|?|GATE|
|MK03.TO.SEPAX.xx.001|?|GATE|

More information about MQ queues used: [https://wiki.swedbank.net/display/DPAY/MQ+Queues]

Some additional original info:
 # Create a keystore if you don’t already have one on your server.
 # Order a Client Auth Certificate, type 5 (if you don’t already have a certificate that you can use.
 ** Here is the link: [https://wiki.swedbank.net/display/mainframeplatform/Order+ssl+certificate]
 # Import your certificate plus the corresponding CA certificate into your keystore (if you didn’t already have it there).
 # Download the RACF CA certificate and import into your keystore: [RACF CA Certificate - Z Integration - Swedbank IT Wiki|https://wiki.swedbank.net/display/ZI/RACF+CA+Certificate] 
 # Enter in the SSL configuration for your application:
 ** CIPHERSUITE (enter only one) and it should be the equivalent of our parameter TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA256
[TLS CipherSpecs and CipherSuites in IBM MQ classes for JMS - IBM Documentation|https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/ibm-mq/9.2?topic=jms-tls-cipherspecs-ciphersuites-in-mq-classes]
CLIENT AUTH = REQUIRED
Protocol:  TLS V 1.2
Peername:  Some Clients need this, depending on the application. If needed, refer to this table: (table.png attached)

Original e-mail conversation with Steven Merry form infra team attached.

column1: [SEPA RB] [DB] Additional info field changes for camt.029 (Recall Refuse)
column47:
*I as* a BO employee *want to* have Additional Information Lines available and new prefixes for Recall refuse *so that* we would be compliant with SEPA rulebook 2023.

Acceptance criteria:
 * If used as a “Negative response to a Recall” (Recall refuse):

 # First occurrence is mandatory and must start with ‘{*}ATR053/{*}’ followed by
the information as per attribute description. This field has to be prefilled and not editable.
 # When refuse reason code is 'LEGL', two further occurrences are allowed to precise the reason and must start with '{*}ATR057/{*}'. This line should be editable.
 # When reason code was ‘FRAD’ in the camt.056, then up to ten further optional occurrences are allowed, all starting with ‘{*}FRAD/{*}’ followed by all information available to file a legal claim to recover the funds in case of reason code ‘Fraudulent originated SEPA Credit Transfer’. All these lines should be editable

 * If used as a Negative Response to the Request for Recall by the Originator” (RFRO Recall Refuse):

 # First occurrence is mandatory and must start with "{*}ATR072/{*}" followed by the information as per attribute description. 
 # When reason code was ‘AC03’ (Wrong IBAN) in the camt.056, then up to ten further occurrences are allowed, all starting with ‘{*}ATR078/{*}’ followed by the information as per attribute description. 

*NB!* Change is required for ST2 and RT1

column1: [iBank] List of payments: Changed account for saved payment creates a duplicate payment
column47:
Changed account for saved payment creates a duplicate payment

Precondition: user has more than one account.

*How to reproduce:*
 * Create a payment (in smart form/foreign, invoice or etc.) and save it to list;
 * Open saved payment in list (Everyday banking -> List of payments);
 * Change "Pay from account{_}"{_} value;
 * Try to  execute it or save it.

*What is wrong:*
 * If user saves this payment, new payment is saved and old (first payment) still remains in list.
 * If user executes this payment - payment still remains in list.

Probably biggest impact is for Einvoices, as user pay the received e-invoice, but invoice stays as unpaid (this case can be only if received einvoice is saved into list and account is changed).

*Expected result could be (need to agree):*

Einvoices:
 * Not allow to change account for einvoice. Account field should be inactive. 
 * -Allow to change account, but fill CREBIT.DP.RELATED_DOC_TYPE_CODE (EINV) and CREBIT.DP.RELATED_DOC_ID (records logic same as for payments).-

Payments:
 * If previously saved payment was executed from different account as it was saved - update existing record (to do not have same, saved payment);
 * If previously saved payment was updated (changes pay from account) - update existing record, not create a new one).

column47:
