There is long list of bank employees in LV and EE plus value Ibank Business for cases when agreement is concluded by customer in iBank; in LT only 1 employee plus iBank Business value.

In every such case local corporate customers representatives have to fill in incident and request to fix the issue.

It should be solved in such way that if employee is leaving the bank then Seller agreement is still possible to open and edit (to change agreement signer from bank side by corporate customer representatives by themselves not involving IT).

{*}When{*}: Any time 
{*}Where{*}: vm.lvmk_odok.vm_odok_dyn procedure (and related procedures and packages) 
*What:* Change mappings for LEI and migrate data

*1. Change LEI mappings from LVMK_DEBT_CRED to DP_ISO*

AS IS:
|*VM.LVMK_DEBT_CRED*|*CREBIT.DP_ISO* |
|LVMK_DEBT_CRED.ULT_DEBTOR_ORG_LEI|DP_ISO.ULT_DEBTOR_LEI|
|LVMK_DEBT_CRED.DEBTOR_ORG_LEI|DP_ISO.DEBTOR_LEI|
|LVMK_DEBT_CRED.CREDITOR_ORG_LEI|DP_ISO.CREDITOR_LEI|

TO BE:
|*VM.LVMK_DEBT_CRED*|*CREBIT.DP* |
|LVMK_DEBT_CRED.ULT_DEBTOR_ORG_LEI|DP.ULT_DEBTOR_ID (DP.ULT_DEBTOR_ID_TYPE:='LEI';DP.ULT_DEBTOR_TYPE:='O')|

*** See also additional info

*2. Migrate existing data from DP_ISO.%_LEI fields accordingly to new mappings.*

Accordingly to pacs.008 format, there can be multiple org_id's present in incoming domestic urgent payments.

All values are stored in LVMK_DEBT_CRED but only one can be mapped to DP. Lets use same priorities as agreed in PAYME-206: {*}COID -> LEI -> TXID -> BIC -> any other from 1st Othr occurrence{*}.

column1: Target2-uploader - Replace SEPAROUTING with EBA RTF (Routing Table File)
column47:
As a Debtor Agent, I want system to automatically upload following EBA RTFs (Routing Table Files) into system, so that data can be used for STEP2 messages routing:
 * Direct Participant (DP) file 
 * Indirect Participant (also named as Reachable BIC (RB)) file

 *Assumptions:*
 # EBA RTF files are distributed usually once per month. Default distribution schedule is previous week Monday prior to STEP2 monthly change date. See [Admission criteria and default rules (ebaclearing.eu)|https://www.ebaclearing.eu/services/step2-t-system/admission-criteria-and-default-rules/]. File transfer from fileshare to Batch portal will be scheduled every Monday at 18:30 CET.
 ** Sterling job (with MAIN ID of transfer 93017) implemented in TEST environment on 22.06.2023 + updated 11.07.2023.

*Acceptance criteria:*
 # Target2-uploader does not upload SEPAROUTING files into system anymore. 
 # Target2-uploader uploads EBA RTF files into system.
See enclosed document for EBA RTF file naming, format, validations, DB table mapping.
 ## Following files are uploaded from Batch portal /sb/sys/data/batch_IO/in/core/target2-uploader_PB/ folder:
 ### Direct Participant file
 ### Indirect Participant file
 ## Files are parsed and data is stored into VM.SR_SEPAROUTING table.
 *** Old records (of either direct participant or indirect participant - depending which while is being uploaded) are deleted from table and new records inserted within same commit. To avoid payment service interruptions, the old records are not deleted when upload is aborted due to errors. 
 *** Any errors that abort the uploaded are reported.
 ## Uploaded files are archived? - to be decided
 # The field comments are updated in VM.SR_SEPAROUTING table according to [^Comments-update.xlsx] (to reflect the changes in the data storing).

*Comments:*
 # Example EBA RTF files attached:
D - Direct participant routing table: [^S204SCTSWEDSESS230327163145D00.T-2023-03-27T16_38_23_916]
I - Indirect participant routing table: [^S204SCTSWEDSESS230327163145I00.T-2023-03-27T16_38_24_217]
 # RT1-uploader for T-type files for reference: [https://git.swedbank.net/projects/DPAY/repos/batch-rt1-uploader/browse]
 # The update of the field comments in VM.SR_SEPAROUTING_LOG table to be handled separately, as we may want to keep both old and new usage rules available in comments with indication of specific date of the logic change.

column1: [Vulnerability] A package installed on the remote host is affected by a remote code execution vulnerability
column47:
h3. Background

Vulnerability related to server lx77174 („Server for C applications development in Baltic Payments area“).

SNAP: [VUL0100889|http://https//snap.swedbank.net/nav_to.do?uri=%2Fsn_vul_vulnerability.do%3Fsys_id%3D1b2f6bcfc38aa91094eb7c94e40131a0%26sysparm_stack%3Dsn_vul_vulnerability_list.do%253Fsysparm_query%253Dactive%253Dtrue]

Path : /sb/sys/opt/oracle/12.1.0/sqldeveloper/sqldeveloper/lib/log4j-1.2.13.jar Installed version : 1.2.13 Fixed version : 2.16.0
h3. Threat

The version of Apache Log4j on the remote host is 1.2. It is, therefore, affected by a remote code execution vulnerability when specifically configured to use JMSAppender.
Note that Nessus has not tested for these issues but has instead relied only on the application's self-reported version number.
h3. Solution

Upgrade to Apache Log4j version 2.16.0 or later since 1.x is end of life.

Upgrading to the latest versions for Apache Log4j is highly recommended as intermediate versions / patches have known high severity vulnerabilities and the vendor is updating their advisories often as new research and knowledge about the impact of Log4j is discovered. Refer to [https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/security.html] for the latest versions.

It is necessary to make additional improvement for the payment rollback proper processing. Partially issue was fixed in _FPAY-506 Incorrect notification after payment rollback - Swedbank._

column47:

As potential solution it was proposed to include for payment storing process to use additional column for unique index check (CREBIT.IX_DP_UK).

*AS-IS:* used it is used Reference and Debtor BIC

*TO-BE:* used Reference+ Debtor BIC + out_channel_code

NOTE: when testing solution need to look also on performance of solution (meaning performance is not decreased)

column636:
28.09.2023 08:50;p998rjs;In abstract e-invoice case overall rule is that in E-invoice XML Invoice record tag sellerRegnumber is filled with operator's registration number and SellerParty record tag RegNumber is filled with original E-invoice issuer’s registration number, i.e. sellerRegnumber in E-invoice is not equal to RegNumber in Seller Party tag.

Please note, that in E-invoice XML in EE and LV it is filled {color:#172b4d}sellerContractId with operator's agreement number and in LT - GlobalSellerContractId.{color}

*EE:*

When intermediary sends abstract e-invoices to the Bank:
 * In Invoice record tag sellerRegnumber is filled with operator's registration number.
 * In SellerParty record tag RegNumber is filled with original E-invoice issuer’s registration number.
 * In whole E-invoice XML where it is used tag {color:#de350b}sellerContractId{color} is filled with operator’s agreement number.

*LV:*

Sending abstract e-invoices in Swedbank’s 1.0 format:
 * In Invoice record tag sellerRegnumber is filled with operator's registration number.
 * In SellerParty record tag RegNumber is filled with original E-invoice issuer’s registration number.
 * In whole E-invoice XML where it is used tag {color:#de350b}sellerContractId{color} it must be filled with operator’s agreement number (long Seller Contract ID).

Sending abstract e-invoices in PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format:
 * In Invoice [ubl:Invoice/cac:AccountingSupplierParty/|https://docs.peppol.eu/poacc/billing/3.0/syntax/ubl-invoice/cac-AccountingSupplierParty/cac-Party/cac-PartyLegalEntity/cbc-CompanyID/]cac:Party/cac:PartyLegalEntity/cbc:CompanyID Seller registration number is filled with operator's registration number.
 * In Seller Party [ubl:Invoice/cac:AccountingSupplierParty/|https://docs.peppol.eu/poacc/billing/3.0/syntax/ubl-invoice/cac-AccountingSupplierParty/cac-Party/cac-PartyLegalEntity/cbc-CompanyID/]cac:Party/cac:PartyLegalEntity/cbc:CompanyID Seller registration number is filled with original E-invoice issuer’s registration number.
 * In whole E-invoice XML where it is used tag {color:#de350b}sellerContractId{color} it must be filled with operator’s agreement number (long Seller Contract ID).

*LT:*

When intermediary sends abstract e-invoices to the Bank:
 * In Invoice record tag sellerRegnumber is filled with operator's registration number.
 * In SellerParty record tag RegNumber is filled with original E-invoice issuer’s registration number.
 * In whole E-invoice XML where it is used tag {color:#de350b}GlobalSellerContractId{color} is filled with operator’s agreement number (long SellerContractID).;;;

column1: Stop SEPA payment messages in Sepa-exchange based on SysGlobal value
column47:
{*}Why{*}: on Friday November 17th after cut-off time for SCT payments, old type of messages should not be sent out anymore, as they will be rejected on Monday morning. Therefore a way to stop forming old format messages is needed.

{*}Where{*}:

{*}What{*}:

Create possibility to stop payment message forming in Sepa exchange. It should be based on SysGlobal.

 

{*}Acceptance criteria{*}:

When SysGlobal is on:
 * domestic SEPA messages are not sent out
 * intrabank payments are working (debited, credited)
 * SCT instant payments are working (debited, credited)

When SysGlobal is switched off:
 * payments done during the time when SysGlobal was on are processed: messages are formed, sent to TPS

*Testing:* only domestic

With new pacs.002 when not all transactions are accepted from bulk, we receive

<GrpSts>PART</GrpSts>

therefore sepa-exchange fails to process pacs.002.

 

Transaction status should be taken from <TxSts> tag.

column1: SLA issue with Standing Order Agreement (SOA)
column47:
For customers who have Standing Order Agreement (SOA) with {*}daily account balance debiting{*}, on weekends and national holidays we are manually modifying the agreement by setting first transaction day to the next working day, because on weekends and national holidays money are just being frozen. Customers are constantly complaining, cases are repeating and repeating.

Relevant for all countries and all customer segments.

*What would at least partially solve the problem* - in STAR and iBank drop down menu add additional option ''Working days only". Please note that there are different national holiday dates in all countries!

There is a logic that calculates next execution day in DB - crebit.per_mk_tootl.leia_arvest_jkp. It uses period code from agreement and setup table crebit.periood to determine next payment date. column1: DB: Standing Order payments after SOA termination should be stopped
column47:
At the moment, the system works as follows: if there is not enough amount on the client's account for a regular periodic payment, the system checks for 3 days (in LT), including the day of payment.

In the same way, the system works after the client terminates the contract on payment date or after the payment date, in the absence of enough money. That is, the system checks the balance for another 1-2 days after the date of termination and debits money when it occurs, since technically the payment hangs in ''pending transactions'.'

This is a bag (Lawyer has confirmed) that should be fixed. After SOA is terminated, all payments should be taken away from ''Pending transactions''.

Change is applicable for LT private and corporate customers.

LV and EE - different functionality. Need to check with country representatives when task is taken.

 

*Note:* possible solution to add additional check if Agreement has been or has been not terminated.

column1: Update SOA payments accepting rules in iBank according to business rules
column47:
Problem from Birute Dainiene: ( INC05588346)

Something is wrong with e-invoices SOA payment day, in case customer was chosen 2 days after receipt of the E-invoice. It’s needed to recheck and solve.

It’s important to have for the customer 2 days because:
1) in all LT documents and e-invoices functionality how it works, we tell the recipient that he can choose 2 days after receipt of the E-invoice, and we show in IB/STAR the day of receiving of e-invoice and the day of payment by SOA. And it should follow 2 days regardless of second accept or other reasons as Pille marked ( see Pille's see explanation below)
2) 2 days are given to customer as his protection against debiting of funds by Bank Products Provision Rules – as in case he would like to recall/cancel this e-invoice presented before debiting of funds;
3) now we have to answer the customer's claim "in my signed electronic payment invoices, the payment date is 2 days after receiving the invoice. I don't understand why you don't comply with the agreement and debiting on the same day." (LT original message: "mano pasirašytose elektroninio apmokejimo saskaitose pasirinkta apmokejimo data 2 dienos po saskaitos gavimo. Nesuprantu kodel jus nesilaikote sutarties ir atskaitete ta pacia diena.")
Customer‘s e-invoices picture from STAR is like this (incorrect debiting in June and August):

( see added documents)

 

Pille's answer was:

the file for the last e-invoice (einvoice nr 01850580) was sent on 04-08-2023 14:19:37 and has been waiting for second accept till 07-08-2023 13:24:06.

SOA payment generator is looking for file creation time and add 2 days to this date.
So, when file sending date is 4.08.2023 then soa payment start date will be 6.08.2023 and end date 8.08.2023.

There accept was done on 7.08.2023 and it is between these days . Immediate processing was because of that.

 

TO DO:

1) Update SOA payment calculation instead of picks einvoice_owner.accept_date instead of einvoice.created_dtime to calculate payment start date.

column642:
07.09.2023 08:25;p998fvu;After discussion with [~birdan] some new things should be explained
Before explanation define:
*Due day* - date that seller defines in a file when importing e-invoices.
*Payment day* - actual date when e-invoice is processed and payment is supposed to be debited.

*Updated*
{color:#FF8B00}Note! Explanations here are done on an assumption that customer must see e-invoice for at least two days before Payment day.{color}

Situation is different in LT/LV and EE.

- LT/LV
Currently in LT and LV import checks that import is done at least 2 days before Due day.
There are three different options for payment day that buyer can choose:
 !screenshot-1.png|thumbnail! 

If we choose to add a validation on a second acceptance that Due day has to be +2 days in a future it will solve the issue for 1st and 3rd option but not for the 2nd. For 2nd option at least 4 days must be left before Due day. Should we expand validation to 4 days to cover that option?

- EE
Currently in EE import does not check Due day and import can be done at any date.
There are 3 different options. What is different about EE is option "During debiting period" if seller has defined debiting period option in a seller agreement:
 !screenshot-2.png|thumbnail! 

If we implement this 2 day validation it will cover 1st and 2nd option but it will not cover debiting period option. In theory, it could only be 100% covered if validation would not allow import/acceptance of file less than 2 days before debiting period start.;;;

11.09.2023 11:16;p998rjs;Summary after meeting with business representatives on 11-09-2023 due to change of e-invoice acceptance validation and error presentment:

1) PB Corporate customer's representatives see that the best solution for them it would be to remove at all acceptance functionality from e-invoice product. Also see that it is related with iBank performance issue [EASYPAY-121] E-Invoices: investigate possible tech solutions for importing of big files in 30 seconds timeout query - Swedbank.

If to implement removal of second acceptance, then it would be needed communication to Sellers in advance before implementing this change to production environment.

2) For LV and LT only: It should be not allowed to accept (nor first, not second acceptance) e-invoice for Seller if it is less than 2 days before due date (2 days should be not hardcoded, but taken according to configuration in system that it is used the same in e-invoice import). It should be agreed which error code to present.

In this case proposal for LT and LV to use error code {*}49{*}: LT error description: The e-invoice payment date is illogical (the PayDueDate is in the past); LV error description: Invalid or incorrect e-invoice payment due date (PayDueDate<=Today+2).

Before implementing this change to production environment it would be needed communication to Sellers in advance, especially those Sellers who are now using acceptance functionality.

In EE no changes are needed: they are fine with 0 days. 

 ;;;
column646:
11.09.2023 14:35;p998rjs;Thanks to [~p998fvu], describing what will happen now when we do not have implemented change for e-invoice acceptance validation from Seller side yet and there is case when Seller has accepted e-invoice later than 2 days before due date:

1) In SOA agreement is set 2 days before due date - payment will be executed +{color:#172b4d}on the same day when e-invoice is accepted{color}+ because it is left less than 2 days before due date. 

2. On due date - payment will be executed on due date.

3. 2 days after e-invoice receiving - payment will be executed on due date, because this date comes sooner than 2 days after e-invoice acceptance.;;;

 * Beneficiary's identification number / registration number
 * Beneficiary's country
 * External payment code

 * Amount of one payment in words
 * Total amount of payments in words

 

Foreign blank, new fields:

column1: (Domestic) Require double accept when beneficiary's account in incoming payment is changed manually
column47:
*Why:*  To decrease operational risk related to change of beneficiary's account

*When:* Any time, latest by SEPA_FLOW_MERGE_START

*Where:* Forms teller/Domestic payments:
 * Incoming faulty
 * Incoming investigation

*What:*  Remove amount limit for double accept so that {*}payments where beneficiary's account is changed manually require always accept from another user{*}. 

 

*Acceptance criteria:*
 # When Beneficiary account is changed manually during incoming payment crediting then payment status is set to 'Incoming faulty for acceptance' (status='D', holder_channel_code='BOA')
 # Payments in status 'Incoming faulty for acceptance' cannot be accepted by the user that changed beneficiary account. 

 

*Comments:*

Beneficiary account can be changed via form “SEPA change IN payment” that can be accessed by clicking [Crediting to account] on following forms {color:#00875a}as an example (there are more routes to that form - via payment/case details, risk screening){color}:
 * “SEPA list of faulty incoming payments” (menu: Operations/Domestic payments/Incoming faulty)
 * “SEPA faulty incoming payments which were sent to investigation”  (menu: Operations/Domestic payments/Incoming investigation)

Account change can be accepted or rejected via form "SEPA accept new account" (menu: Operations/Domestic payments/Incoming faulty).

This is existing functionality except that currently, domestic payments require accept only when payment amount is over double acceptance limit (pkontor.smkpiir based on branch of the user). In Foreign Payments system there is no amount limit and all payments with changed account require accept. It was agreed to remove limit also from Forms teller as the number of such transactions is very low and risk is high. The change can be done at any moment, no need to link it to SEPA FM activation date.

It would be preferred not to update the limit in a/m table column (pkontor.smkpiir ) to 0 as this limit might be used for some other purposes also. Better to remove limit check for this specific feature and always require accept. 

 

*Note for BA / APO:* When starting, inform business to update process in ABC ([R-15430)|https://earchive.swedbank.net/cs/idcplg?IdcService=CMS_DOWNLOAD_LATEST_WEBFILE&xDocumentNumber=R-15430]

column1: EBA RTF upload - Change in file pattern check
column47:
*WHY:* There is a need for small change in EBA Routing Table File (RTF) file name pattern check. 

Currently the pattern check it too strict which excluded some files from automatic upload. Maintenance persons had to manually change the file names. 

Examples of recently received files:
 * S204SCTSWEDSESS231207163145D00.T-2023-12-07T16_38_17_792
 * S204SCTSWEDSESS231207163145I00.T-2023-12-07T16_38_17_878
 * S204SCTSWEDSESS240209163146D00.T-2024-02-09T16_38_33_180-COPY
 * S204SCTSWEDSESS240209163146I00.T-2024-02-09T16_38_33_387-COPY
 * S204SCTSWEDSESS240226163145D00.T
 * S204SCTSWEDSESS240226163145I00.T

*WHERE:* Target2-Uploader -> RTF Upload

*WHAT:* EBA RTF file name pattern check is changed to *ignore symbols after Z (if any)* and accept these files for upload.

EEVVSSSBBBBBBBBYYMMDDHHMMssNNN.Z
||File name position||Description||Example||
|EE|Always S2.|S2|
|VV|VV is format version.|04|
|SSS|3-letter service identifier.|SCT|
|BBBBBBBB|BIC(8) of the Direct Participant.|SWEDSESS|
|YYMMDDHHMMss|File creation date and time (Coordinated Universal Time - UTC).|230327163145|
|NNN|1{^}st{^} character is D or I:
·       D – Direct Participant
·       I – Indirect participant (reachable BIC)
Next 2 are incremental number starting from 00 that is reset to 00 every time the file creation date and time (YYMMDDHHMMSS) changes.|D00
I00|
|Z|Type of file. T = RTF|T|
|-Symbols after Z-|-YYYY-MM-DDTHH_HH_MM_SSS-
-Timestamp of downloading the file-|-2023-03-27T16_38_23_916-|

column1: SEPA exchange: need to separate Instant payments RuleBook sysglobal
column47:
Currently both SEPA and Instant payments new rulebook changes are turned on by common sysglobal SEPA_RB2023_DATE. As instant payments RT1 test environment is already with rulebook changes, it does not accepts old format instant payments anymore so we need instant payments to be sent always in new format in TEST environment. SEPA payments can be tested in both formats, so in TEST environment SEPA_RB2023_DATE sysglobal is being changed constantly to before rulebook and after. This disturbs instant payments work in TEST and causes a lot problems especially during regression testing not only for our team but for some other teams in bank also who is using instant payments functionality. Therefore need to be able to send instant payments always in new format not depending on SEPA_RB2023_DATE sysglobal.

Liberty property shall be added, which would allow bypassing current rulebook check. If bypass enabled, then sysglobal SEPA_RB2023_DATE shall be ignored for RT1 XMLs, otherwise - SEPA_RB2023_DATE shall be checked. Property can be found and changed in bootstrap file for each country and environment (e.g. [https://git.swedbank.net/projects/LIBERTY/repos/sepa-exchangelv_vm/browse/config/TEST/bootstrap.properties#140]). Bypass is disabled in PROD and enabled for all other environments.

*Issue:* Before Rulebook 2023 changes, there were no strict requirements for structured address fields in iBank domestic payment form. Now min. Country + Town must be filled.

If historic/defined payment has only Country filled, then user will have to add Town, when initiating new payment from historic/defined payment.

*Preconditions:*

column1: [DB] to create new algorithm for service id
column47:
Vilniaus šilumos tinklai wants to check the service ID, according to an algorithm. This algorithm should be implemented till 01.11.2024

new algorithm for service id :

Vilniaus šilumos tinklai pageidauja įsidėti šį algoritmą e.sąskaitų prašymuose pateikiamo mokėjimo kodo tikrinimui. 

 
 # a) Jei Kliento kodas prasideda raide „V“, Kliento kodą turi sudaryti „V“ + 6 skaitmenys. .
 # b) Jei Kliento kodas prasideda skaičiumi, Kliento kodą turi sudaryti 7 skaitmenys ir Kliento kodas turi turėti tokią struktūrą:

X1X2X3X4X5X6K, kur X1 – X6 – Kliento kodo skaičiai, K – kontrolinis skaičius. Kontrolinis skaičius apskaičiuojamas: sumą X1*7 + X2*6 + X3*5 + X4*4 + X5*3 + X6*2 + Z*2 padalinus iš 11 (vienuolikos), kontrolinis skaičius yra liekana, gauta atlikus dalybos veiksmą. Jeigu gauta liekana yra lygi 10 (dešimt) arba 0 (nulis), tada kontrolinis skaičius 0 (nulis). Čia Z – Vilniaus regiono kodas (1), t. y. Z = 1. Pavyzdys, kaip apskaičiuojamas kontrolinis skaičius: jei Vilniaus regiono Kliento kodo 6 pirmi skaičiai yra 315660, tai: 3*7 + 1*6 + 5*5 + 6*4 + 6*3 + 0*2 + 1*2 = 96; gauta suma dalinama iš 11, gaunami 8 sveiki ir liekana 8; pilnas Kliento kodas yra 3156608.

column1: (SEPA-Exchange) Send intragroup payment message pacs.008 (CT)
column47:
*WHY:* Intragroup payment messages are not sent to beneficiary bank via SEPA infrastructure, but are routed directly via ProSwitch together with appropriate accounting in Swedish side. 

*WHERE:* In SEPA-Exchange, when intragroup (out channel code = 'SEPGO') payment has been submitted to outgoing queue.

*WHEN:* After date & time defined with sysglobal SEPA_FLOW_MERGE_START. No need to restrict the functionality with the sysglobal, intragroup payments with out channel code 'SEPGO' shouldn't appear earlier.

*WHAT:* 
 # Intragroup payment must follow different cut-off time ([https://jira.swedbank.net/browse/PAYRUN-1285]) than defined for domestic and cross-border SEPA payments and stop the payment (holder_channel >> 'CUT') in case sending after cut-off is not allowed
 # Create payment messages (pacs.008.001.08) as usual
 ## Assign new processing flow code 'GF' to intragroup messages
 # Wrap outgoing messages into the proprietary ProSwitch header as done currently in SEPA-Transfer
 # Send intragroup messages to ProSwitch by putting them to the existing outgoing queue used by SEPA-Transfer
 # Set message straight to final status after processing the proprietary response from ProSwitch. 2nd response from EBA is not expected in this flow:
 ## in case of positive response: initial status 'S - Sent' becomes 'A - Accepted', there is no intermediary status 'B - In Bulker' used
 ## in case of error: S > E ? (check how it is done in SEPA-Transfer today)
 ## in case of negative response: S > N ? (check how it is done in SEPA-Transfer today)
 # Currently SEPA-Transfer is saving incoming messages also into the filesystem - it should be sufficient if SEPA-Exchange could just log them.

*Expected results:*

Intragroup SEPA payment messages (pacs.008) are not sent out through TPS Gateway, but through ProSwitch reusing same MQs as currently in SEPA-Transfer.

column1: (SEPA-Exchange) Receive intragroup payment message pacs.008 (CT)
column47:
*WHY:* Intragroup payment messages are received from ProSwitch where they skip SEPA infrastructure and are directly routed from sender to beneficiary bank, together with appropriate accounting in Swedish side. 

*WHERE:* In SEPA-Exchange, when intragroup payment message (pacs.008.001.08) has been received in incoming queue from ProSwitch.

*WHEN:* After date & time defined with sysglobal SEPA_FLOW_MERGE_START. Before that date & time intragroup messages must be processed by SEPA-Transfer, still.

*WHAT:* 
 # Listen and receive messages from the existing incoming queue used by SEPA-Transfer today
 # Unwrap messages from the proprietary ProSwitch header and process messages as usual
 # Assign processing flow code 'GF' to intragroup messages
 # Calculate correct out channel code according to payment data, cannot assign 'SEPGI' automatically, since there can also appear old cross-border (non-intragroup) payments which were held in Proscan during the flow merge go-live!

*Acceptance criteria:*

1. Incoming payment is saved in DP with following out_channel_code:
 * Cross-border payment (BIC country is not local country and BIC is not intragroup BIC) - 'SEPCI'
 * Intragroup payment (BIC is intragroup BIC (HG_SWIFT_LIST)) - 'SEPGI'

2. Creditor reference validation is not done for cross-border and intragroup payment; only done for domestic

3.{color:#172b4d} Check also service_limitation -> we should check cross-border and intragroup with 'FPI', not 'LPC'{color}

{color:#172b4d}4. Any other validations are same as for incoming domestic payments.{color}

column1: (TEST) Return incorrect incoming intragroup payment
column47:
*Probably only testing is needed!*

 

*WHY:* It is needed to *auto-return incoming intragroup SCT* when it cannot be credited due to pre-agreed reasons, or it is needed to *manually initiate return of incoming intragroup SCT* when payment cannot be credited. 

*WHEN:* From SEPA_FLOW_MERGE_START

*WHERE:*
 * Automatic return in SEPA-Exchange
 * Manual return in 'SEPA return incoming payment' form (accessed via [Making return] from Domestic payments > Incoming name control / Incoming faulty / Incoming investigation menus)

*WHAT:* 

Applicable when incoming intragroup pacs.008 is received and is in status suitable for returning ('D' + holder_channel 'BOF','BOI','BON'). 

Main functionality/changes to return incorrect cross-border SEPA payments have been implemented with PAYME-503 [CORE DB] Send pacs.004.001.09 (RETURN) for incorrect incoming x-border payment - Swedbank

Additionally, with outgoing intragroup return messages it is needed to :
 # Intragroup return payments must follow different cut-off time ([https://jira.swedbank.net/browse/PAYRUN-1285]) than defined for domestic and cross-border SEPA return payments and stop the return payment (holder_channel >> 'CUT') in case sending after cut-off is not allowed
 # Assign new processing flow code 'GF'
 # Wrap messages into the proprietary ProSwitch header as done currently in SEPA-Transfer
 # Send messages to ProSwitch by putting them to the existing outgoing queue used by SEPA-Transfer
 # Set message straight to final status after processing the response from ProSwitch. 2nd response from EBA is not expected in this flow:
 ## in case of positive response: initial status 'S - Sent' becomes 'A - Accepted', there is no intermediary status 'B - In Bulker' used
 ## in case of error: S > E ? (check how it is done in SEPA-Transfer today)
 ## in case of negative response: S > N ? (check how it is done in SEPA-Transfer today)

 

*Acceptance criteria:*

1. When incoming intragroup pacs.008 cannot be credited due to pre-agreed reasons then system creates return payment automatically.
 * Pre-agreed reasons: select error_code from crebit.dp_error_st2  where AUTO_RETURN_INDICATOR ='Y' 

2. User can manually create return payment for incoming intragroup payment by clicking [Making return] on different forms in Forms teller:
 * "SEPA incoming payments which require manual check" 
 * "SEPA list of faulty incoming payments"

column1: Create general PL/SQL interface to close Standing Order Agreements in case it is closed payer account
column47:
*Why:*
 * According to GDPR (TIDY program) it is planned to send Standing Order (SO) agreement's data to MDM Agreement summary for Global Data Disposal orchestration. Therefore it must be ensured that in case any automated bank process or employee closes bank account it is not left any active SO agreements. 
 * Currently in automated Negative Account service closing/customer of-boarding/ NAB process SO agreement closure is not included.  
 * Left open SO agreements might impact wrong calculation of business relationship end date with the customer on Global Disposal Mechanism side (end date would be prolonged) as such agreements are closed at next standing order payment that depends on set by customer SO periodicity (after day, week, month, quarter, half year or even after a year). 

*When:* as soon as possible.

*Where:* DB stored PL/SQL procedures related with SO agreements (table crebit.per_mk)

*What:*
 # Prepare interface to close SOA and orders for provided account so that Negative Account service closing/customer of-boarding/ NAB process and other automated processes could use it for initiation of agreement closure.
 # In case it is closed payer account (crebit.per_mk_ANR) by NAB or any other automated process or manually in database automatically check and close active and waiting for authorization SO agreements that have status (STAATUS): 'A' (Authorized/ Active) or ’O’ (Waiting for authorisation/ in preparation) and orders. Procedure should be run daily.

*WHY:* It is needed to send claim non-receipt for outgoing intragroup SCT.

 # Assign new processing flow code 'GF'

 # Wrap messages into the proprietary ProSwitch header as done currently in SEPA-Transfer
 # Send messages to ProSwitch by putting them to the existing outgoing queue used by SEPA-Transfer
 # Set message straight to final status after processing the response from ProSwitch. 2nd response from EBA is not expected in this flow:
 ## in case of positive response: initial status 'S - Sent' becomes 'A - Accepted', there is no intermediary status 'B - In Bulker' used
 ## in case of error: S > E ? (check how it is done in SEPA-Transfer today)
 ## in case of negative response: S > N ? (check how it is done in SEPA-Transfer today)

*Acceptance criteria:*

column1: (SEPA-Exchange) Receive camt.027 (CL_RECEIPT) for intragroup pacs.008
column47:
*WHY:* To process claim non-receipt related to incoming intragroup SCT. 

*WHERE:* In SEPA-Exchange, when intragroup claim non-receipt (camt.027.001.07) has been received in incoming queue from ProSwitch.

*WHEN:* At least from SEPA_FLOW_MERGE_START. Can be available earlier, since such messages are not travelling through ProSwitch nor processed by SEPA-Transfer currently.

 # Listen and receive messages from the existing incoming queue used by SEPA-Transfer today
 # Unwrap messages from the proprietary ProSwitch header and process messages as usual
 # If related incoming intragroup SCT message is not found with intragroup flow code ('GF'), then search under x-border flow code ('FF') as well, it might be from pre-flow-merge era.
 # Assign processing flow code 'GF' to intragroup messages

*Acceptance criteria:*

 # User can view camt.027 message basic data by clicking [Message details] in “SEPA message chain" or "SEPA case details" form.

column47:

-list MQ queues to be accessed by newly ordered channels

column1: [DB] Create new Oracle tables for DAY0 loading
column47:
It is necessary to *create* a new table "{*}MDM_INITIAL_AGREEMENTS{*}" inside a new "PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM" schemas (PAYRUN-1349) of CORE DB (LT, LV, EE).

This table will be used for initial DAY0 Loading (transfer of all agreements data from products).

The new table must contain the following columns:
||New columns names||Field type||Description||
|product_name|VARCHAR2(35)|Product system name source ('STANDING_ORDER_AGREEMENT', 'GIRO_BENEFICIARY_AGREEMENT', 'BANK_DEFINED_PAYMENT_AGREEMENT')|
|agreement_id|NUMBER|Engagement number|
|status|VARCHAR2(1)|Engagement status|
|dt_from|DATE|Engagement start (activation) date|
|dt_till|DATE|Planned or actual engagement end date|
|last_updated_time|TIMESTAMP|Exact timestamp of when change happened|
|account_id|VARCHAR2(35)|Account id|
|customer_id|VARCHAR2(8)|Party id|
|ready_for_sending|VARCHAR2(1)|Indicator for DAY0 load procedure:  'Y' - ready, can be taken for sending; 'N'  - not ready; 'S' - sent|
|placed_in_aq_dt|DATE|Date when DAY0 load procedure proccessed message (placed it in AQ)|

It means, that we send them directly for debiting, skipping initial validation.
4. By canceling FPO payments, we set status 'N' and error_code 'H0020' in case this value was empty.

column639:
13.03.2025 10:32;p998osm;Description of Status criteria:
1. Authorized - status I and value_date is current date and holder_channel_code is null or AUTH for FPO/TPHCO payments   
2. Future value date - status I and value_date is in future date and holder_channel_code is null or AUTH for FPO/TPHCO payments   
3. Additional processing ALL (Faulty) - status I or D and holder_channel_code is BO and eror_code is not null
4. Additional processing DUPLICATE (Problematic) - status I and holder_channel_code is BO and eror_code is H0011 or H0054 
6. Waiting for funds - status I and holder_channel_code is REP or for FPO/TPHCO it could be FPOB with error_code A0014
7. In processing - status D or ( status I for instant payments with holder_channel_code SPX or other payments with holder_channel_code SPC)
8. Processed - status C
9. Cancelled - status N
10. 100K Eur limit EU sanctions for RU/BY nationals - status D and error_code T0016 and holder_channel_code BO
11. Waiting in channel - status I and dp_out_thn.channel_status E or A;;;

1) According to GDPR (TIDY program) requirements aligned with PB lawyers it must be stored all Account alias consents for 10 years after consent termination:
 * [EE and LV lawyers input on retention rules for Account alias consents.|https://wiki.swedbank.net/download/attachments/1821816202/RE%20Tidy%20retention%20rules%20%20Alias%20.msg?version=1&modificationDate=1704194310000&api=v2]
 * [LT lawyer input on retention rules for Account alias consents.|https://wiki.swedbank.net/download/attachments/1821816202/RE%20Tidy%20retention%20rules%20%20Alias%20%20%281%29.msg?version=1&modificationDate=1704194311000&api=v2]
 * [Account Alias PB TIDY application assessment.|https://workspaces.swedbank.net/sites/TIDY/_layouts/15/WopiFrame2.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B08A703F0-F3C9-453C-9998-D117571DF075%7D&file=Account%20Alias%20PB%20TIDY%20Application%20assessment%20template_1.5_2022xlsx.xlsx&action=default&IsList=1&ListId=%7B25615F05-0142-42C7-82AE-9D85EE983B86%7D&ListItemId=1625]
 * [Summary of Baltic Payments area products data retention/ deletion rules.|https://wiki.swedbank.net/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=2030189620#expand-SummaryofBalticPaymentsareaproductsdataretentiondeletionrules] 

2) As it is stated in agreement conditions with LT Central bank according to their request Swedbank should be able to provide Account alias consent's data for 10 years after their termination. 

3) Currently in database table account_alias.alias are stored only active consents. In case consent is terminated then consent data is immediately removed from account_alias.alias table. Historical information is possible to extract from log table account_alias.alias_log.

4) It was taken decision to integrate Account alias consents with MDM AgrSum for Global data destruction orchestration, therefore we have to store consent termination dates and historical consent data are needed for initial data loading.  

*When:* as soon as task will be prioritized for implementation.
*Where:* Schema: ACCOUNT_ALIAS, account alias consents main table: ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS. Account alias log table: ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS_LOG.  
*What:*

1. Implement new separate archiving table ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS_ARCH with the same fields where it would be stored only revoked consents. Leave currently existing logic that in table ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS are stored only active consents. Leave current procedure which is automatically removing consent record from ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS table when consent revoked/ cancelled. 

{color:#172b4d}2. On database level implement trigger which additionally would create record in ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS_ARCH table when consent is revoked and would fill consent termination date in field VALID_UNTIL and change STATUS='REMOVED'. {color}
 * {color:#172b4d}_Note:_ Currently in table ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS it is used only one status value: 'ACTIVE'. But overall we found 3 statuses: 'ACTIVE', 'REMOVED', 'WAITING_CONFIRMATION'. Agreed to use status 'REMOVED' with meaning as consent closure/ termination/ revoke (checked with iBank team that this status is not used, see Jira task: [https://jira.swedbank.net/browse/MB-2645]). {color}{color:#000000} {color}

3. In tables ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS, ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS_LOG  and ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS_ARCH implement field 'ID' that would be used to identify unique consent number.
 * Currently record uniqueness is defined by two fields 'TYPE' (always filled with value 'PHONE') and 'ALIAS' (phone number). But in fact customer can several times give and revoke consent (difference is in seconds only) for the same or other account number.
 * From AgrSum integration point of view it is demanded to have unique record number.

4. Fill historical records of terminated consent's data in table ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS_ARCH based on information stored in table ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS_LOG where 'LOG_ACTION'='D' (Deleted): fill status '{color:#172b4d}REMOVED{color}', fill consent termination date 'VALID_UNTIL', also add unique numbers for consent records.
 * {color:#172b4d}_Note:_ Until February 2025 when account alias is revoked, in ACCOUNT_ALIAS.ALIAS_LOG table field VALID_UNTIL was filled. {color}{color:#172b4d}After February'2025Y this field VALID_UNTIL is left as empty.{color}
 ** {color:#172b4d}In both cases status is still left as 'ACTIVE' and LOG_ACTION='D'.{color}
 ** {color:#172b4d}On 14th of January'2026 discovered this change and in E-pay team had discussion regarding field VALID_UNTIL filling logic and agreed to leave as is, i.e. field will not be filled in case account alias is revoked.{color}

column1: [DB] Fill in agreement termination dates in all closed E-invoice related agreements
column47:
*Why:* Agreement end dates are required to send to MDM Agreement Summary (if taken decision to integrate with MDM) or will be used in local data disposal mechanism. Also termination date will be used for start counting agreement retention date. 
 * It is planned to send agreement's data to MDM Agreement summary all non-closed agreements including the ones created earlier than 2007.01.01 and all active and closed agreements which are closed >= 01.01.2007. E-invoice service was launched in PB after 2007Y, therefore all data is in scope.
 * Seller agreements, table einvoices.seller_agreement: in LT: 2 agreements that are closed (status='C') do not have filled end_date.
 * E-invoice operator service agreements, table einvoices.seller_destination_agreement, LT: 28 agreements; LV: 1; EE: 29 closed agreements do not have end date.
 * E-invoice automated payment agreements, table einvoices.payment_agreement: LT: 123; EE: 7 closed agreements do not have end date. 

*When:* Until implementation of Agreement summary integration.

*Where:* In PB Core database.

*What:*

column1: [DB] Implement new fields for LV Bank defined payment agreements/ templates
column47:
* *Why:* New fields are required to send to MDM Agreement Summary and start counting agreement retention date.
 * *When:* Until implementation of Agreement summary integration.
 * *Where:* In *LV* Core database table crebit.tyyp_mk where are stored Latvian Bank defined payments agreements/ templates.
 ** No need to implement new fields in Estonia and Lithuania although both countries have such table and were using typical payments functionality in STAR (After clarification with EE and LT business received request to close all active typical payments templates and not to present this functionality in STAR at all as it was very rarely used). 
 * *What:* Implement new fields for *Latvia* only:
 ** CREATED_BY: audit field, user name who created record. 
 ** CREATED_DTIME: audit field, date and time when record was created. 
 ** START_DATE: agreement start date. 
 ** END_DATE: agreement end date. 
 ** {color:#172b4d}CUSTOMER_AGREEEMENT: Y/N. Filled manually. In case record is created based on signed agreement with corporate customer then value 'Y', if created based on bank's own initiative, then should be marked value 'N'. {color}
 *** {color:#172b4d}No specific agreement numbers are assigned to customer related agreements by business, only date. TM_LEP_NR can be used as unique identifier to be sent to Agreement Summary.{color}
 ** CUSTOMER_ID: customer CORE ID. Mandatory. Should be filled manually.
 *** {color:#172b4d}Agreed with LV business representative on rule that for LV bank defined payments templates/ agreements in case of customer merge/ join/ acquisition they would always close old agreement and open new instead of changing existing agreement. {color}
 ** Accordingly it should be created fields in log table.
 * LV: Implement automated field filling with help of triggers:
 ** CREATED_BY: mandatory, fill user name who created record when new record is created.
 ** CREATED_DTIME: mandatory, fill date and time when new record is created.
 ** KES (LAST_MODIFIED_BY): make mandatory to fill, fill user name who last modified record.
 ** MILLAL (LAST_MODIFIED_DTIME): make mandatory to fill, fill date and time when last user has modified record.
 ** START_DATE:  mandatory. By default pre-filled with record creation date when new record created.

column1: [DB] 16. Track changes in agreements for Account alias
column47:
Create a sysglobal *MDM_TRACK_ALIAS* (LT, LV, EE Core DB) that will allow to enable (Y) or disable (N) tracking of changes in account_alias agreements.

Create trigger 
* on *account_alias.alias* table to track insert/update changes of id, status, valid_from, valid_until, customer_id. (LT, LV, EE DB)
* on *account_alias.alias_arch* table to track delete operation. (LT, LV, EE DB)

In case tracking of Account alias is enabled (sysglobal *MDM_TRACK_ALIAS* value is *'Y'* ) call procedure payments_agreements_mdm.mdm_payload_message_generation.*mdm_agreement_alias* (EASYPAY-1471).

+Input parameters:+

* i_operation - VARCHAR2, possible values: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE;
* i_agreement_id - NUMBER, account_alias.alias.id
* i_status - VARCHAR2, account_alias.alias.status
* i_dt_from - DATE, account_alias.alias.valid_from
* i_dt_till - DATE, account_alias.alias.valid_until
* i_last_updated_time - TIMESTAMP, cast account_alias.alias.last_modified_at to timestamp
* i_customer_id - VARCHAR2, account_alias.alias.customer_id

column1: [DB] 17. Payload messages generation on MDM requests for Account alias
column47:
Create 2 new procedures *ENGAGEMENT_PULL_ALIAS* and *ENGAGEMENT_LIST_PULL_ALIAS*  in a new package *PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.MDM_INCOMING_REQUEST* (PAYRUN-1515) in CORE DBs (LT, LV, EE) 

New procedures must be able to:

* Select product agreements data based on input parameters
* Format selected agreement data to Engagementpayload message format (to call procedure *PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.MDM_PAYLOAD_MESSAGE_GENERATION.MDM_AGREEMENT_ALIAS* described in EASYPAY-1471)

+Input parameter+ for *ENGAGEMENT_PULL_ALIAS*:

* i_source_ref - unique engagement source reference account_alias.alias.id

+Input parameters+ for *ENGAGEMENT_LIST_PULL_ALIAS*:

* i_status - NULL or [value]. If a value is provided select data from account_alias.alias.status
* i_last_modified_dtime - NULL or [value]. If value is provided - all engagements modified from this date (account_alias.alias.last_modified_at) to be re-generated.

----
{color:#DE350B}Note: for MDM request we collect data as from alias table as from alias_arch!!!  {color}
----
 

*Examples* from other product areas:

[EngagementPullpayload|https://wiki.swedbank.net/display/BCD/Topic+payloads#expand-EngagementPullpayload]
{code:java}

The new procedure must be able to:
 * select a batch of product agreement data from PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.{*}MDM_INITIAL_AGREEMENTS{*} table (PAYRUN-1420) where *ready_for_sending = Y* and {*}type='ACCOUNT_ALIAS_AGREEMENT'{*};
 * for each selected record to call procedure PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.MDM_PAYLOAD_MESSAGE_GENERATION.{*}MDM_AGREEMENT_ALIAS{*} (EASYPAY-1471);
 * for each sent record to set PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.{*}MDM_INITIAL_AGREEMENTS.placed_in_AQ{*} = (database sysdate) and set *ready_for_sending = S* (meaning record is created in AQ table)

column1: [FLM | Validate and Enrich] LV Regulatory reporting enrichment for Homebank/MX
column47:
*Why:* Foreign bank customers may not be able to provide BOP data as required in Swedbank MIG.  In current Homebank (POP) MT101 flow, all payments that require BOP code are repaired manually by adding general '379' code. Manual processing is not part of the new MX (pain.001) flow design. Instead of rejecting payments, system should populate pre-agreed values. 

*Where:* Payment services - FlmSupportingService/ValidateAndEnrich

*What:* 
{panel}
*Only in LV, for Homebank payments (in_channel_code='POP'):*
 * When residency country is required but missing (error L111?) then assign DP.CREDITOR_RES_COUNTRY value as follows:
 ** In case of intrabank payment (CRE) -> creditor's residency from bank system
 ** In case of other payment types, first of:
 *** Creditor Postal Address Country
 *** Creditor IBAN country
 *** Creditor Agent BIC Country (from derived BIC, if applicable; otherwise from message)
 *** Creditor Agent Postal Address Country
 * When BOP code is required but missing (error H0174?) or wrong then set  DP.BOP_CODE value to "379", do not give error.

! No change for other channels (e.g. SGW) ->  do not enrich, continue to give errors.
{panel}
*Acceptance criteria:* 
For payments in amount over BOP limit (see below):
 # When residency country is not provided under _RegulatoryReporting/Details/Country_ and {_}Creditor/CountryOfResidence{_}, then DP.CREDITOR_RES_COUNTRY is taken from Creditor Postal Address Country OR Creditor IBAN Country OR Creditor Agent BIC Country OR Creditor Agent Postal Address Country (in given order);  no error about missing residency country is returned.
 # When _RegulatoryReporting/Details/Code_ is filled with valid BOP code, then DP.BOP_CODE is filled with provided value (no enrichment).
 # When _RegulatoryReporting/Details/Code_ is not provided or incorrect value is provided, then DP.BOP_CODE is set to "379"; no error about missing/invalid BOP code is returned.

For payments under BOP limit, enrichment of BOP information is not done. 

*Testing notes:*
 * Payment balance code (BOP code) is mandatory if one of the parties (Debtor or Creditor) is a resident and the other party is a nonresident, and payment amount is or exceeds 10 000 EUR (or equivalent amount in other currency).
 * Residency country of debtor is taken from customer data.
 * Residency country of creditor is taken from pain.001 in following order: 1) RegulatoryReporting/Details/Country, 2) Creditor/CountryOfResidence

column1: [FLM | Validate and Enrich] EE Creditor Reference enrichment for Homebank/MX (local payments)
column47:
*Why:* Foreign bank customers may not be able to provide Creditor reference under Structured Remittance Information since this is not widely used worldwide.  In current Homebank (POP) MT101 flow, all payments that have issues with Creditor Reference are repaired manually (mostly successfully). Manual processing is not part of the new MX (pain.001) flow design. Instead of rejecting payments, system should enrich/repair creditor reference whenever possible, instead of rejecting payment. 

*Where:* Payment services - FlmSupportingService/ValidateAndEnrich

*What:* 
{panel}
*Only in EE, for Homebank payments (in_channel_code='POP')*
 # CRE, SEPO, SIPO, RTGS: If Creditor Reference *is present but does not match to reference format* requirements (RF standard, Estonian standard or beneficiary's specific rules) then MOVE value to Unstructured Remittance Information and continue processing. Exception: if reference number is mandatory for beneficiary but invalid then reject payment. 
 # CRE: If Creditor Reference is *not present but it is mandatory* for beneficiary then analyze text within Unstructured Remittance Information field and identify the *first valid Estonian creditor reference number* that appears as a {*}standalone, delimiter‑separated numeric value{*}. Embedded or partial matches inside continuous digit sequences must not be considered.
 ## When valid Estonian Creditor Reference is found and it matches to beneficiary's reference number requirements then COPY the value to Creditor Reference and continue processing.
 ## When valid Estonian Creditor Reference is not found or it does not match to beneficiary's reference number requirements then reject payment.{panel}
*Acceptance criteria*

*1. Creditor reference is provided*
 # CRE, SEPO, SIPO, RTGS: If a Creditor Reference is present but does not meet RF standard, Estonian standard or beneficiary‑specific rules, then it is treated as invalid.
 # If a Creditor Reference is invalid but mandatory accordingly to beneficiary‑specific rules , then payment is rejected.
 # For other cases, if a Creditor Reference is invalid, then the value is moved into the Unstructured Remittance Information and payment processing continues.

*2.  Creditor reference is mandatory but not provided*
 # If the Unstructured Remittance Information does not contain a standalone, delimiter‑separated digit sequence with a valid Estonian reference then payment is rejected
 # If the Unstructured Remittance Information contains a standalone, delimiter‑separated digit sequence with a valid Estonian reference and it meets the beneficiary’s reference number rules, then the value is copied to the Creditor Reference and payment processing continues.
 # If the Unstructured Remittance Information contains a standalone, delimiter‑separated digit sequence with a valid Estonian reference but it does not meet the beneficiary’s reference number rules, then payment is rejected. 

*Testing notes*
 * Examples of valid creditor references: 123; 2800082268; 10111152162678; RF78123; RF78000000000000000000123
 * Examples of invalid creditor references: 1234; 211100615745; 12345678901234567890; RF123; RF7800000000000000000012
 * Customer specific rules are described in crebit.ref_number
 * See also [ReferenceNumberEnrichment_examples.xlsx|https://myntet.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/teams/PaymentsBaltic/Delade%20dokument/Analysis%20and%20architecture/Homebank%20MX%20Payment%20Initiation/Testing/ReferenceNumberEnrichment_examples.xlsx?d=wa7f3119137034bbca502b43ab6c8fdc0&csf=1&web=1&e=XkEd9z]

column1: [FLM | Validate and Enrich] LT Creditor Reference enrichment for Homebank/MX (local payments)
column47:
*Why:* Foreign bank customers may not be able to provide Creditor Reference under Structured Remittance Information since this is not widely used worldwide.  In current Homebank (POP) MT101 flow, all payments that have issues with Creditor Reference are repaired manually (mostly successfully). Manual processing is not part of the new MX (pain.001) flow design. Instead of rejecting payments, system should enrich/repair creditor reference whenever possible, instead of rejecting payment.

*Where:* Payment services - FlmSupportingService/ValidateAndEnrich

*What:*
{panel}
*Only in LT, for Homebank payments (in_channel_code='POP'):* 
 # SEPO, SIPO, RTGS:  If Creditor Reference is *not present but it is mandatory* for beneficiary and Unstructured Remittance Information contains *valid Creditor Reference* as the only value then MOVE the value to Creditor Reference and continue processing. 
 # CRE: When Creditor Reference is *not present but it is mandatory* for beneficiary then analyze text within Unstructured Remittance Information field and look for the *valid Creditor Reference* that appears as a {*}standalone alphanumeric value{*}. Embedded or partial matches inside continuous sequences must not be considered.
 ## When valid Creditor Reference is found then COPY the value to Creditor Reference and continue processing. In case of multiple matches, copy first.
 ## When valid Creditor Reference is not found then reject payment.{panel}
*Acceptance criteria:* 
 # For SEPO, SIPO, RTGS:
 ## If Creditor Reference is not present but it is mandatory and Unstructured Remittance Information contains valid reference number as the only value then he value is moved from Unstructured Remittance Information to Creditor Reference and payment processing continues (no error about missing reference number).
 ## If Creditor Reference is not present but it is mandatory and Unstructured Remittance Information contains valid reference number but it is not the only value then Remittance Information is not changed and payment is rejected due to missing creditor reference. 
 ## If Creditor Reference is not present but it is mandatory and Unstructured Remittance Information does not contain valid reference number then Remittance Information is not changed and payment is rejected due to missing creditor reference. 
 ## If Creditor Reference is not mandatory, then Remittance Information is not changed and payment processing continues (no error about missing reference number).
 ## If Creditor Reference is present and it is mandatory but it does not contain correct code then payment is rejected.
 ## If Creditor Reference is present and it is mandatory and it contains correct code then payment processing continues.
 # For CRE:
 ## If Creditor Reference is not present but it is mandatory and Unstructured Remittance Information field contains valid creditor reference within the text, then reference value is copied to Creditor Reference, Unstructured Remittance Information is not changed, and payment processing continues. 
 ## If Creditor Reference is not present but it is mandatory and Unstructured Remittance Information field contains multiple valid creditor references within the text, then first reference value is copied to Creditor Reference, Unstructured Remittance Information is not changed, and payment processing continues. 
 ## If Creditor Reference is not present but it is mandatory and Unstructured Remittance Information field does contains valid creditor reference, then Remittance Information is not changed and payment is rejected due to missing creditor reference.
 ## If Creditor Reference is present and it is mandatory but it does not contain correct code then payment is rejected.
 ## If Creditor Reference is present and it is mandatory and it contains correct code then payment processing continues.

 

*Testing notes:*

column1: [FLM | Validate and Enrich] Creditor Reference enrichment for Homebank/MX (FPO)
column47:
*Why:* We are currently not supporting structured creditor reference for international payments. For SEPA cross-border payments, creditor reference is allowed. In current Homebank (POP) MT101 flow, all payments that have issues with Creditor Reference are repaired manually (mostly successfully). Manual processing is not part of the new MX (pain.001) flow design. Instead of rejecting payments, system should enrich/repair creditor reference whenever possible, instead of rejecting payment. 

*Where:* Payment services - FlmSupportingService/ValidateAndEnrich

*What:* 
{panel}
*For Homebank payments (in_channel_code='POP') - EE, LV, LT*
 # SEPCO, SEPGO, SIPCO: If Creditor Reference *is present* then keep it as Creditor Reference and continue processing.
 # FPO: If Creditor Reference *is present* then MOVE value to Unstructured Remittance Information and continue processing.{panel}
*Acceptance criteria*
 # SEPCO, SEPGO, SIPCO: If a Creditor Reference is present then it stays as Creditor Reference and payment processing continues.
 # FPO: If a Creditor Reference is present then value is moved into the Unstructured Remittance Information and payment processing continues.
 

{*}Note{*}: It might be decided to allow creditor reference in international payments in future, depends on VDE19-459 analysis result. Then this change will have to be reverted...

column1: BH: Refactor payment orders sending to FLM
column47:
*Why:* For reliable and reusable sending to Kafka new table is needed, to be used later in scheduler for sending messages to Kafka
*When:* 
*Where:* core-payment-batch-handler-data-manager
*What:* 
 # Update how payments are created in Bhandler database:
 ## When inserting them to payments table - use status "P_PROCESSING"
 ## When inserting them to payments table - also insert data to table EVENT_OUTBOX (created with EASYPAY-1553)
 # Create scheduler which will
 ## Take messages from table EVENT_OUTBOX (created with EASYPAY-1553) in batches of 500. With event_type SEND_PAYMENT_ORDER
 ## Lock the messages (so that other instance would not get them)
 ## Publish them to Kafka topic  w990.batch.handler.payment.orders
 ## On successful publishing update messages in EVENT_OUTBOX: status to COMPLETED, SENT_AT to current dtime
 ## Implement retries if sending to Kafka fails - update message in EVENT_OUTBOX - update RETRY_COUNT and NEXT_RETRY_AT (should be current_dtime + retry_count*5 sec)
 ## If max_retries is hit, update message status to "FAILED"
 # Remove code:
 ## Updating payment status
 ## Publishing payment to Kafka (in red in the diagram)

 

For inserting data to EVENT_OUTBOX table:
 * EVENT_TYPE = SEND_PAYMENT_ORDER
 * EVENT_OBJECT_SID = PAYMENT.SID
 * PAYLOAD - Kafka message payload
 * STATUS - PENDING

column1: [DB] Create a new field customer_id for Standing order agreements
column47:

*Where:* PB Core database, table: crebit.per_mk.  

*What:*

 * Add a new field named customer_id to the table crebit.per_mk and all related log/arch tables in the databases: core, arch, and lexus.

*Testing Notes*

 * Create new agreements and update existing ones via STAR and iBank systems:

column1: iBank: update signing via list of payments - store session information
column47:
*Why:* if payments are signed via list of payments, they need to be sent for fraud screening. Fraud screening will be initiated via Batch handler
*When:* under sysglobal PAYRUN-2711
*Where:* private and corporate iBank
*What:* 
When payments are being signed from list of payments, for all payments getting last signature (one in case no double signing is needed, two - in case double signature is required), signing session information has to be stored.

For each mass payment in the list of payments:
 * store signing session information to table PAYMENTS.BATCH_SESSION_INFO created with PAYRUN-2655.
 * store header id in table PAYMENTS.BATCH_SESSION_INFO
 * for each payment in mass payment store batch session SID to PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_REFERENCE table with related_system_code = 'SESSION_ID'

For all not-mass payments in list of payments::
 * store signing session information to table PAYMENTS.BATCH_SESSION_INFO created with PAYRUN-2655.
 * for each payment store batch session SID to PAYMENTS.PAYMENT_REFERENCE table with related_system_code = 'SESSION_ID'

Functionality has to work the same with below mentioned sysglobals on and off:
 * CH_PMT_LIST_ONLINE_EXEC_COUNT
 * CH_PMT_LIST_ONLINE_VALID_COUNT

column1: [IBank]: If changes made in payment uploaded via SGW - new payment must be created instead of initial one
column47:
*Why:* Currently, if customer has uploaded the payment file via Swedbank Gateway it is saved in List of Payments. If customer modifies information in the payment, in pain.002 is sent back information that settlement on the debtor’s account has been completed for all payments in payment information block (ACSC).  Currently there is no information for customer that payment data has been changed. In separate story it is described that there should be visible a warning message for customer (EASYPAY-998) in case customer makes some changes.

*When:* using sysglobal created with 

PAYME-1496

**
*Where:* in Corporate IBank - Everyday Banking - List of payments. The exact payments were uploaded via Swedbank Gateway. The in_channel_code is "HGW", because that means that payment was imported via Swedbank Gateway.

There can be opened such payment forms:

 - in SMART form (Domestic and European payments),

 - in International form (if International payments),

 

*What:* If customer has uploaded not signed payment via Swedbank Gateway it is visible in List of payments.

It is needed to develop so that if customer opens the payment and modifies any of the fields in the payment form and saves or approves the payment:
 # New payment:

 * There should be  created a new payment instead with the same details and with the made changes. For the new payment should be used the same parameters as, if the payment has been crated in SMART form or in  International form.
 * The new payment should be created and stored in CREBIT.DP table with appropriate status.

2. Initial payment (Payment that was in the file):
 * {color:#172b4d}The final status in CREBIT.DP should be changed to N{color}
 * {color:#172b4d}In pain 002{color} <OrgnlPmtInfAndSts><PmtInfSts> (Payment Information Status) should be RJCT with  
<Rsn> <Cd> (Reson code): PAYRUN-3161 Cancelled by client. New payment created by user in internetbank.

 
*Note!* If it is customer who modifies the payment, then all requirements above are valid. If it is bank itself (for example, intrabank name check) then the requirements above are not valid and no changes are needed.

 

 

Comment: Mass/Salary payments are not covered under this Jira task. Information about them will be added separately under
 * PAYRUN-2995
 * PAYRUN-3000

 

 

*Translation labels (if any):* none

*Possible impacts (changes could impact other applications/ processes etc.):* Text
*Acceptance criteria/ testing notes:* If not signed payment file is uploaded via Swedbank Gateway and the payment is modified, in CREBIT.DP the initial payment must be visible with status N (rejected) and there should be visible a new payment with new payment ID.

The original payment that was uploaded via Swedbank Gateway, should also be visible in CREBIT.DP, but with status N.

 * for each sent record to set PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM.{*}MDM_INITIAL_AGREEMENTS.placed_in_AQ{*} = (database sysdate) and set *ready_for_sending = S* (meaning record is created in AQ table)

Termination date should be taken from log table from field 'CHANGED_DATE'/ 'LOGDATE' (which field to use will be decided during development) of the record where in field 'STATUS' was removed value 'A' or 'B' and field left empty/ null value.

column1: Ignore Interbank settlement date if provided in future for Incoming instant payments.

*Why:*  Swedbank started receiving instant payments “with future” date from some market participants.

It is strange situation as currently leads to situation that payment is credited to customer only after some days not instantly. Also, Swedbank Liquidity positions are updated on moment when payment received what makes difference on our comparison reports.

*When:*  At any moment (sooner better)

*Where:* SEPA Exchange

*What:*   Instant payment must be made available to customer immediately. Ignore the value date (Interbank settlement date, XML tag <IntrBkSttlmDt>) from SCT Inst message when setting DP.VALUE_DATE and set it to current date

(?) Or maybe it is more correct to use date from AccptncDtTm?

(?) Should same rule be applied also for REMIT_TRN_VD, BENEF_TRN_VD, DOC_DATE?

*Acceptance criteria:*
 * Correct incoming instant payment with IntrBkSttlmDt in future is credited on the same day when it is accepted (current date).
 * Correct incoming domestic payment with IntrBkSttlmDt in future is credited on the date specified as IntrBkSttlmDt (future date)

 

*Possible impacts (changes could impact other applications/ processes etc.):* 

To ensure change is implemented *ONLY* for SEPA instant flow and do not impact SEPA Normal message processing

column1: iBank Private and Business PB: Re-factor error and warning messages behavior when Instant Payment Limits are reached
column47:
*Why:*
 * The *result to implementation* of the two *specific logics* for iBank Private and Business PB:
 ** (EASYPAY-1107) _Automated switch of Payment priority "Instant" to "Ordinary"/"Economy" in SMART payment form in case customer has disabled/exceeded instant payments limit_
 ** (EASYPAY-1195) _Showing warning messages in case customer disabled instant payments or exceeded instant payment, daily and/or monthly limits in SMART payment form_
 * *Two {color:#FF0000}issues{color}* were discovered
 ** *1.1 Instant Payments limits reached* hides Instant Payment warning and informative message, where expected to be: 
!image-2025-09-24-13-20-44-651.png!  
 ** *1.2 Instant Payments Disabled* hides Instant Payment warning and informative messages performed, where expected to be:  
!image-2025-09-24-13-22-41-444.png!{*}{*}{*}{*}
 ** *The reason behind this issue is known* 
 *** Front end sending *information* that some fields were changed on form
 *** That *triggers* another Payment Limit Service call 
 *** It checks for account and agreement limits removing initial warnings and errors
 ** *2. Change of payment amount*
 *** Upon ** reaching Instant Payment Limits or Disabled ** Instant Payments ** user try to change amount back to available Instant Payment Limit, but Payment Priority Stays the same

*When:*  It was agreed that this task can be implemented before IPR Go Live after {color:#172b4d}5th{color} of October 2025.
*Where:* In iBank Private and Business -> Daily banking -> New payment -> tab: "Domestic or European", SMART payment form
*What:*  The existing logic should be corrected.
 * *If* Instant Payment Limits reached or Instant Payment is disabled
 ** *change* payment priority to Regular and show corresponding warnings and informative warnings (EASYPAY-1195)
 ** *If* account or agreement limits also reached
 *** *show* together with Instant Payments warning and informative message
 *** *hide* forward button (Sign with SmardID) 
 ** *If* account or agreement limits are not reached
 *** *show* Instant Payment warnings and informative messages
 *** *don't hide* forward button (Sign with SmartID)
 ** *If* user change the payment amount and it's *within* allowed Instant Payment Limit or Enables Instant Payment
 *** The payment priority should automatically *change back* to Instant

 

*Translation labels:* No changes with labels.
*Possible impacts (changes could impact other applications/ processes etc.):*

column1: PB Implement automated E-invoice Seller Agreement and Operator Service agreement closure if agreement was not activated during 6 months
column47:
*Why:*
 * According to GDPR (TIDY program) requirements aligned with PB lawyers it must be implemented data retention/ destruction rules for E-invoice service related agreements: Seller Agreements and Operator Service Agreements if agreement was not activated during 1 year:
 ** [Baltic E-invoices TIDY application assessment|https://workspaces.swedbank.net/sites/TIDY/Shared%20Documents/DB%26IT/BB%20Consumer%20Payments/Approved/TIDY%20Application%20data%20retention%20assessment_E-invoice.xlsx?d=w1927bc3247694bc7ac65d748ea6d01c1].
 ** [PB lawyers approval.|https://wiki.swedbank.net/download/attachments/1821816202/RE%20Tidy%20retention%20deletion%20rules%20final%20verification%20for%20E-invoices.msg?version=2&modificationDate=1698675176000&api=v2]
 ** [Summary of Baltic Payments area products data retention/ deletion rules.|https://wiki.swedbank.net/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=2030189620#expand-SummaryofBalticPaymentsareaproductsdataretentiondeletionrules]
 * Business representatives have decided that it is more efficient to have implement automated processes for such agreements with status 'I' (Inserted) tracking and closure.
 * It is planned to send E-invoice Seller agreements data to MDM AgrSum for global data disposal orchestration. Operator Service agreements data will be disposed locally. 
 * With product business representatives agreed that Seller agreements with inserted status 'I' should be terminated after 6 months, then from GDM AgrSum side this agreement data will be deleted after 6 months (in total after 12 months after record creation).    
 * It is planned to send agreement's data to MDM Agreement summary all non-closed agreements including the ones created earlier than 2007.01.01 and all active and closed agreements which are closed >= 01.01.2007.
 * From MDM Agreement Summary side it will be tracked status change from ’I’ (Inserted) ->’C’(Closed) and it will be possible to apply different data retention calculation and retention rule than for generally applied rule when agreement status is changed from 'A' (Active) -> ’C’(Closed).
 * According to test database currently there are Seller agreements: EE 4; LV: 1, LT: 1, and Operator Service Agreements LT: 1 with status ’I’ (Inserted) that were created more than 1 year ago.

*When:* Until implementation of Agreement summary integration.

*Where:* In PB Core database tables:
 * Seller Agreements: einvoices.seller_agreement.
 * Operator Service Agreements: einvoices.seller_destination_agreement: 

*What:*

1. PB:  implement automated Seller Agreements and Operator Service Agreements closure processes for agreements:
 * Search for agreements that were created more than 6 months ago;
 * Change status: ’I’ (Inserted) ->’C’(Closed); 
 * Frequency of automated process running: monthly.

2. PB: it should be also closed currently existing agreements with status ’I’ (Inserted) status to 'C' (Closed) that were created more than 6 months ago:
 * Seller agreements: EE 4; LV: 1, LT: 1.
 * Operator Service Agreements: LT: 1.

*Possible impacts (changes could impact other applications/ processes etc.):* 

*Acceptance criteria/ testing notes:* 
 # Run automated process and test in db if Seller agreements and Operator Service Agreements with status 'I' that were created more than 6 months ago status was changed to 'C'.
 # Check if it was changed status to 'C' for old agreement records:

 * Seller agreements: EE 4; LV: 1, LT: 1.
 * Operator Service Agreements: LT: 1.

column1: [E-invoice] configuring dedicated data source in Core from Payments side with specific timeout settings
column47:
*As part of iBank resilience program it is required to reduce database transaction timeout to 30s in order to speed-up application self-recovery.* 
Requirement is connected to the risk: [https://snap.swedbank.net/now/nav/ui/classic/params/target/sn_risk_mitigating_actions.do%3Fsys_id%3Df62980d397203d104f5fffb3f153af0d%26sysparm_record_target%3Dsn_risk_mitigating_actions%26sysparm_record_row%3D7%26sysparm_record_rows%3D7%26sysparm_record_list%3Du_risk%253D607c28251bc7659035a9edb1b24bcb2f%255EORDERBYnumber]

In order to meet this requirement E-invoice import functionality in the iBank should be improved.

-To have an ability to reduce Oracle database query execution timeout for common connection pools in order to have resilient internetBank we can use one of approaches to allow large e-invoices to be usable.-

-It can be solved by creating dedicated datasource/connection pool with bigger timeout just for e-invoices functionality or by setting bigger query execution timeout just for e-invoices functionality.-

iBank transaction timeout is set on JTA level via Atomikos transaction manager. Since iBank does not support custom transaction definitions, the only way to change transaction timeout is end native transaction before file import and importing file in a new transaction with an extended timeout.

This solution should be considered as temp solution/workaround, proper solution should be delivered later.

column1: [DB] Create log table for payload messages that were send to MDM
column47:
It is necessary to *create* a new table "{*}MDM_OUTGOING_MESSAGES_LOG{*}" inside a new "PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM" schemas (PAYRUN-1349) of CORE DB (LT, LV, EE).

This table will store payload messages that were send to MDM.

The new table must contain the following columns:
||Field name||Field type||Description||
|source_type|VARCHAR2(35)|Source engagement type (STANDING_ORDER_AGREEMENT, GIRO_BENEFICIARY_AGREEMENT,BANK_DEFINED_PAYMENT_AGREEMENT)
|agreement_id|NUMBER|Engagement number from source system|
|correlation_id|VARCHAR2(30)|Unique event correlation Id from source system. Will be used to communicate about message processing error|
|payload_message|CLOB|Payload message in JSON format|
|sent_date|DATE|Date when payload message was sent to MDM|

 Partitions by {*}sent_date{*}: 1 week length, keep length 5

*Add* for role payments_mdm_role (PAYRUN-1360) to INSERT records in this table

column1: [DB] Create new table to store copy of incoming MDM requests
column47:
Create a new Oracle table "{*}MDM_INCOMING_REQUESTS_LOG{*}"

||New columns names||Field type||Description||
|request_date|DATE|Database system time of record insertion|
|request_type|VARCHAR2(30)|Message type: 'ENGAGEMENT_PULL', 'ENGAGEMENT_LIST_PULL' (coming from MDM)|
|source_ref|VARCHAR2 (80)|Unique engagement source reference (sourceRef). Format: <shema_name>.<table_name>[<unique record_id>].|
|engagement_type|VARCHAR2(50)|NULL or [value]. If value is provided - specific engagement type: STANDING_ORDER_AGREEMENT, GIRO_BENEFICIARY_AGREEMENT,BANK_DEFINED_PAYMENT_AGREEMENT|
|engagement_status|VARCHAR2(50)|NULL or [value]. If value is provided - specific engagement status.|
|source_last_modified_time|TIMESTAMP|NULL or [value]. If value is provided - all engagements modified from this date to be re-generated|
|destination_topic|VARCHAR2(60)|Kafka topic that should received data. For example "agreement-summary-change".|
|request_payload|CLOB|Copy of original JSON request from MDM system|
|request_status|VARCHAR2(10)|'COMPLETED', 'FAILED'|
 
Place the new Oracle table under "PAYMENTS_AGREEMENTS_MDM" schema (PAYRUN-1349)


Partitions by *request_date*: 1 week length, keep length 5

Add for role payments_mdm_role (PAYRUN-1360) to INSERT copy of payload messages in this table

column1: [TEST]  pdf in STAR
column47:
Currently Egde is configured based on old STAR requirements:

!image-2024-10-18-09-10-20-065.png|width=713,height=177!

Why it is not OK :
 # This option will cause all PDF downloads under user „Downloads“ folder located in „C:\Users%USERNAME%\Downloads“ and the folder is not automatically cleaned in the background, therefore there could be violations within GDPR requirements.
 # This option is not the default option within MS Edge browser (the default value is „Off“ or „Disabled“), therefore web-services that are used within MS Edge will need to adapt to the custom option, where all PDFs are downloaded to user „Downloads“ folder, instead of PDF presenting within MS Edge browser view (main reason is GDPR violation, because files are not cleaned automatically). It is not possible programmatically to switch the option to OFF via web-service, every user needs to configure it by themselves via Edge UI to “OFF”.

In order to avoid unneeded downloads on PC it is required to have such view:

!image-2024-10-18-09-11-26-863.png|width=746,height=188!

*Action for those ones who are using pdf in STAR, please:*
 # change manually configuration in Edge to this:

!image-2024-10-18-09-12-07-959.png|width=733,height=185!

2. check your functionality which is using PDF. Make sure that new configuration is not braking it.
